By Saikat Mandal | 20 Nov 2026 13:41, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 20:10.

Arsenal have reportedly joined Real Madrid in the race to sign Bayern Munich winger Michael Olise.

The 24-year-old joined Bayern in the summer of 2024 from Crystal Palace and has established himself as one of the finest wingers in European football.

The Frenchman has scored 54 goals and provided 61 assists in 122 appearances, although even those phenomenal numbers do not fully reflect what he brings to the Bayern side.

During the summer transfer window, Real Madrid were heavily linked with a move for Olise, but Bayern made it clear that the winger was not for sale at any price.

Bayern have reportedly placed a £265m valuation on Olise, who is under contract at the Allianz Arena until 2029.

However, club CEO Herbert Hainer has made it clear that no such asking price has been set for the player, whom they want to keep for many years to come.

According to Christian Falk, Arsenal are among the clubs interested in Olise, although it could prove difficult for the Gunners to prise him away from Bayern.

If Olise does decide to leave Munich, a move to La Liga could make more sense, having already experienced life in the Premier League.

There is also a significant gap between Olise's earnings and those of Harry Kane at Bayern, and the German club are expected to do everything in their power to convince the winger to sign a newly introduced contract.

The Bild journalist mentioned: "Every club has Michael Olise on their shortlist. There’s a lot of respect for Arsenal, but there are some really significant players at the table, like Real Madrid.

"Olise has already played in the Premier League, so I strongly suspect a move to La Liga would be the next logical step were he to look for a move away from Munich.

According to recent reports, "That all stated, Bayern Munich have proven that significant personal awards like the Ballon d’Or can still be won at FC Bayern. So, that’s the hope of the club and they’ll do everything in their power to keep Olise at the Allianz Arena.".

Olise could still be tempted to stay at Bayern after seeing his club teammate Harry Kane win the Ballon d'Or this year.

A move to a more competitive league could appeal to the Frenchman, while he may also want to join a club where his chances of winning the Champions League are high.

Bayern have not set an asking price for Olise and could demand a staggering fee, with paying such an amount likely to be nothing short of madness.

Arsenal arguably need a right winger who can provide reliable cover for Bukayo Saka rather than a player of Olise's calibre, who would expect to be a guaranteed starter if he made the move to the Emirates Stadium.

Leicester have decided to end their deal with controversial sponsors BC.GAME six months ahead of schedule.

Fans expressed fury and dismay earlier this month after the club's unlicensed gambling shirt sponsor appointed an 'international porn star' as its new ambassador.

Now Leicester have opted to conclude the partnership – in a move welcomed by supporters. A statement on Wednesday read: ‘The decision follows constructive discussions between both parties in recent days, during which we recognised our differing commercial priorities moving forward.

‘We would like to thank BC.GAME for its support throughout its two-and-a-half-year association with Leicester City and for the constructive approach taken in reaching this agreement.

‘Supporters who have purchased a BC.GAME-branded replica shirt through official LCFC retail channels within the last 28 days (since 21 October, 2026) can return it for a full refund or exchange (subject to availability) by Wednesday 2 December.’.

Recent findings suggest that BC.GAME, an online casino company, had been the Foxes' primary shirt sponsor since the start of the 2024-25 season. They announced a partnership with Russian adult content creator Eva Elfie in a video on X earlier this month.

Leicester City have axed a partnership with BC.GAME, after the gambling shirt sponsor appointed 'international porn star' Eva Elfie as its newly introduced ambassador.

Leicester confirmed fans who have purchased a replica shirt featuring the sponsor's name within the last 28 days can return it for a full refund or exchange by December 2.

Elfie, who has 4.8million Instagram followers, is known in Esports and gaming communities too.

In recent years, Leicester’s spectacular decline on the pitch has mirrored the relationship with their supporters.

During the years immediately before and after their stunning Premier League triumph in 2016, it was difficult to find a club more in tune with the fanbase.

But a series of baffling decisions – including the tie-up with BC.GAME – eroded trust between the club and their supporters.

Leicester are now in League One and face a long road back but sensible moves like this one suggest they are at least facing in the right direction again.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 20 Nov 2026 14:06, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 14:06.

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has confirmed a quadruple injury boost for his side ahead of Sunday's blockbuster Premier League battle with Manchester United at Anfield.

The Reds have the honour of hosting Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge of the Red Devils, in which they will endeavour to improve on a paltry record of just one win from five home matches in the 2026-27 top flight.

Liverpool maintained their excellent away form by beating Crystal Palace 3-1 before the international break, but Dominik Szoboszlai emerged as an injury worry following the Selhurst Park success.

The midfielder nevertheless joined up with Hungary for the November international break and played the full 90 in both of their Nations League games against Georgia and Northern Ireland, supplying two assists against the former.

Szoboszlai was managing a knee problem during his time with the Magyars, but speaking to the media on Friday, Iraola affirmed that the 26-year-old will be fine for Sunday's main event.

"He's in a good place, he's playing normally, he was not even strapped today so he's fine yes," Iraola responded when asked if Szoboszlai was still being carefully looked after.

As well as confirming Szoboszlai's availability, Iraola delivered positive updates on the Dutch trio of Ryan Gravenberch, Jeremie Frimpong and Virgil van Dijk.

The latter withdrew from the Netherlands squad for the November window due to an unspecified fitness problem, while Gravenberch and Frimpong were both absent from the win over Palace.

Frimpong sustained a hamstring injury against Brentford in October and has missed Liverpool's last six games in all competitions, while Gravenberch has been dealing with a minor heal fracture.

However, all three are in line to feature against old rivals Man United, as Iraola added: "If everything goes to plan they should be available for the game.

It has been revealed that "Gravenberch, it's a matter of pain, he's managing but he's been training the last two days. Jeremie is recovering the same. We've introduced him with the rest of the group, and Virgil is fine to go.".

Should all of Szoboszlai, Van Dijk, Gravenberch and Frimpong make the cut, Liverpool's only remaining concerns are the long-term trio of Conor Bradley, Giovanni Leoni and Hugo Ekitike.

The latter is still a while away from making a full recovery from an Achilles injury, but Leoni and Bradley have returned to team training as they close in on returns from serious knee injuries.

Recent findings suggest that however, Iraola confirmed that neither defender will be in the squad on Sunday, adding: "The international break was the best moment to introduce them slowly, they've started doing things with the team. They are still not available, but it's very good news and I hope they can play in some weeks.".

Liverpool sit fourth in the Premier League table with 18 points from their opening 10 games, but they have won just two of their last nine matches against Man Utd.

West Ham’s Home Advantage Problem Won’t Disappear With 60,000 Fans

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (420 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Claretandhugh

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mark Noble has called on West Ham United supporters to help transform the London Stadium into an intimidating venue as Scott Parker prepares for his first home match in charge against Preston North End.
  • Speaking in an interview with the club’s official website, Noble praised the ‘extraordinary’ loyalty of West Ham fans following relegation and insisted that the club’s ambition remains an immediate return to the Premier League.
  • He also challenged supporters to make life uncomfortable for visiting teams, arguing that a crowd of 60,000 should give West Ham a significant advantage.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mark Noble has called on West Ham United supporters to help transform the London Stadium into an intimidating venue as Scott Parker prepares for his first home match in charge against Preston North End.

Speaking in an interview with the club’s official website, Noble praised the ‘extraordinary’ loyalty of West Ham fans following relegation and insisted that the club’s ambition remains an immediate return to the Premier League.

He also challenged supporters to make life uncomfortable for visiting teams, arguing that a crowd of 60,000 should give West Ham a significant advantage. But I think it’s crucial to point out that getting the fans onside and creating an intimidating atmosphere are probably two very different things.

There’s no doubt about it. When the London Stadium is loud, it is impressive, as anybody who attended that incredible night against Sevilla will testify.

But I do think it’s a long way from being intimidating.

For that to happen, I firmly believe supporters need to be close to the pitch.

Not just to cause opposition players discomfort, but to put pressure on referees and give West Ham the kind of home advantage that seems prevalent throughout the league.

The distance between the stands and the playing surface remains a fundamental problem, regardless of how many supporters are in attendance.

It’s something I’ve previously argued when discussing proposals to improve the stadium atmosphere.

Isolated tiers in the stadium and poor pitch proximity do little to help the atmosphere at the London Stadium.

It was always my concern that relegation to the Championship would see visiting teams regard a trip to the London Stadium as a lovely day out in opulent surroundings. Opposition changing rooms are grand and palatial and their team coach can pull into the venue untroubled by home fans.

And our results in Stratford have certainly done little to disprove that theory. However, that doesn’t mean things can’t improve.

I genuinely believe that getting West Ham playing on the front foot will help eliminate some of the eerie silences we’ve heard so frequently at the London Stadium.

Noble wants supporters to see a team giving everything, and I think he’s absolutely right about that.

If Parker can produce an aggressive, attacking side that gives the crowd something to get excited about, the atmosphere should improve considerably.

But turning the London Stadium into a genuinely intimidating venue is another matter entirely.

And unfortunately, that’s a problem which can’t be solved simply by asking 60,000 people to make more noise.

All that money spent and Spurs do not have a proper striker or goalkeeper

⏱️ ~30 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that for all the money spent, Tottenham Hotspur have started this season without a reliable out-and-out striker and short of a top goalkeeper.
  • Industry observers note that we keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing?
  • Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that for all the money spent, Tottenham Hotspur have started this season without a reliable out-and-out striker and short of a top goalkeeper. And it is already costing them dear.

Industry observers note that we keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing? Maybe not since his Bournemouth days.

Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.

It is a puzzle how Tottenham signed 10 newly introduced players, but did not upgrade two of the most important positions on the pitch.

Industry observers note that only when Aston Villa were out of sight and the game was effectively over did Spurs break their Premier League goal drought. And even then it was a midfielder, Conor Gallagher, and a defender, Jan Paul van Hecke, who were on target.

Solanke had gone off just before Villa scored their second goal, which highlighted the significant difference between the two sides on Saturday and where Spurs are badly lacking.

It has been revealed that zion Suzuki, the Villa goalkeeper, rolled out a long ball upfield, Nicolas Jackson managed to lay it off for Johan Mazambi, who returned the favour. Jackson touched the ball past Micky van de Ven’s challenge before beating Kinsky with a well-struck shot.

Spurs are stunned as Nicolas Jackson doubles Aston Villa's lead 😳📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/il7NKbgFCQ.

Industry observers note that it was an excellent goal, but Kinsky got a good hand to it and a top goalkeeper would have pushed it around the post. On the evidence of the first half, when he made four saves, Suzuki would have also stopped the ball creeping into the net.

Suzuki cost Villa in the region of £30m and he looks a more than able replacement for Emiliano Martínez. Spurs, on the other hand, have not had a top-class goalkeeper since Hugo Lloris and it is a puzzle that so much faith has been placed in Kinsky.

Sources indicate that spurs spent most of the summer firmly denying any links to Jackson before Villa signed him from Chelsea for an initial £47.5m that could rise to £65m. Given the London club paid an initial £75m for Sávio and committed to a £60m obligation to make Omar Marmoush’s season-long loan permanent, Jackson might have been a relative bargain for them.

Asked if Tottenham had made a big mistake by failing to sign a proper number nine, head coach Robert De Zerbi mentioned: “The transfer market was long. The situation changed many times. There was also the financial rules, at the end of the transfer market. And we had to respect the rules.

“We didn’t sell the players who we thought, in the beginning, there was the possibility, the chance to sell. There are a lot of reasons. I think the club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players, we know everything. And if we didn’t make any different decisions, it was because we couldn’t.”.

Recent findings suggest that that sounded a bit like excuses, but De Zerbi did not put up much of a defence for Solanke as he remarked: “We need more from him, for sure, but he’s one of my players. I like Dom as a player and I stay with him until the end. He needs to stay better, to feel better. The physical condition is not good enough, but it’s normal for him. Maybe he is not confident enough in himself at this moment, because he’s much better than this. I think we can’t say everything is bad, but it’s not enough.”.

According to recent reports, it was Sávio who forced Suzuki into making a brilliant double save from him in the first half, when Tottenham were well on top. The Japan international also stopped an Archie Gray shot from squirming through his legs and into the net, and dived to turn another Sávio effort around his right-hand post.

In a recent development, jackson was not the only Villa fresh boy who upstaged Tottenham’s expensive new attackers. Manzambi not only assisted for Jackson, but also marked his first start for the Midlands club with a goal that put the visitors ahead in first-half stoppage time.

Johan Manzambi is off the mark for Aston Villa, and what a time to do it! ⚽️📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/rLRbbUM4Jm.

Andrew Robertson will have been disappointed with his attempt to clear the ball, John McGinn played it into the path of Boubacar Kamara and his scuffed shot fell into the path of Manzambi, who found the back of the net.

Substitute Mohammed Kudus was correctly denied an equaliser following a VAR check before Jackson’s goal and a brilliant strike from Emiliano Buendía that effectively clinched a first league win of the season for Villa.

Emi Buendia, that is a BEAUTIFUL strike 😮‍💨📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nNplbL7mpd.

Unai Emery, the head coach, spent years watching Martínez and Ollie Watkins win games for Villa with decisive actions, and is hoping this was evidence that Suzuki and Jackson can do the same for him.

Sources indicate that “They are here for it [making the same impact],” Emery remarked. “His commitment, Zion is really very good. His commitment, Nico Jackson as well is fantastic. But every player needs to understand how we can feel better collectively, how they can help us with their qualities, and how we can collectively exploit our best performance.

Industry observers note that “Today we made one clear step forward. Zion is keeping his performance like he did before. Jackson today clearly improved his performance. This is the way forward and the example for the other players.

“Manzambi played a good match, but he’s not yet understanding everything we need on the field with our positioning. He’s a fantastic player and must feel free playing to try to exploit himself and his qualities. But, of course, always under our structure.”.

Speaking after the match, former Spurs man Joe Cole was critical of the club’s summer business which has left them without an out-and-out goalscorer and a weak defence.

"You can't rule them out of a relegation battle"Steven Gerrard and Joe Cole have major concerns for Spurs 😬🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/JivM5pNfM9.

It is definitely fair to say that this season has not started the way either of these teams would have wanted, as the host side at the moment sit in what is apparently their favourite position – 17th – and the visitors are all the way in 19th, only above Coventry.

Despite getting off to a fairly convincing start in the Champions League with a 3-2 win over Club Brugge, Villa only scored their first league goal last week in their match against Nottingham Forest, though it was a futile one as they still lost 2-1 at Villa Park.

Tottenham meanwhile are still waiting for their first league goal, despite putting one past Liverpool in their 3-1 defeat in the Carabao Cup third round. With no European football and already out of one cup competition, Roberto De Zerbi has only the FA Cup in January and the rest of the league season to drag Spurs out of the perpetual rut they appear to find themselves in. They sit only one point above Villa as they have been able to see out two 0-0 draws – against Everton and Nottingham Forest – instead of one.

It has been revealed that there has been plenty of talk about the money spent by both teams, without the results yet to show for it. The total sits around half a billion between them, adding to the mounting pressure on both De Zerbi and Unai Emery. Summer signings for both teams have struggled to land, something which will not be helped by the upcoming international break.

But before then, the teams have 90 minutes to try and get their seasons up and running, and we will be bringing you the team news, lineups and all the action from the match! Stay tuned!

Scaroni has been the face of the stadium project for many years, and he was a guest at a sports talk organised by RCS and entitled ‘Attracting foreign capital and enhancing the system for a real relaunch’.

He spoke alongside Giovanni Carnevali (CEO and General Manager of Juventus), Giuseppe Marotta (President and CEO of Inter) and Ezio Maria Simonelli, (President of the Lega Calcio Serie A). His words are via MilanNews.

Serie A seems to be struggling compared to other Italian sports. What could be done to make football more competitive?

“You’re telling me about something we’re doing, Gerry Cardinale’s idea. He came to the world of Italian football after twenty-five years in sport.

“It’s about creating Milan Sport Entertainment, that is, creating other sports around Milan, combining other sports with football, providing entertainment, communicating, and using Milan and Milano – because he also places great importance on the city of Milan, which is one of Europe’s emerging cities – to create an attractive environment for other sports and other situations.

“I’ll give just one example: if you take the United States, which is a gigantic market for the world of sports, football comes in fifth among the sports that Americans love, after basketball, of course, and even after hockey.

According to recent reports, “This is the idea that Gerry brought in Italy, coming from his vast experience in the world of sport, and therefore around this we look to our future. Gerry Cardinale comes to say that he will never sell Milan, precisely because his project is a long-term one.”.

The Generali Stadium will be something more than a stadium and will help this….

It has been revealed that “Let’s say it’s been quite a complex journey. A very long one that I’ve been on with Inter since 2018-2019. But we’ve reached, let’s say, some key milestones. The first was in November last year, when we bought the San Siro stadium.

“The Meazza belongs to Inter and Milan, and the entire surrounding area. So every now and then I read debates: ‘But should it be torn down, shouldn’t it be torn down?’. Well, this will be a decision we’ll make because it’s ours, so I want to say: we have a clear, notarial fact behind us that gives us ownership of the San Siro stadium.

“This was the first step. The second was the presentation of the stadium that we held a few weeks ago. Sources indicate that “Building a great stadium like this is something extremely important. Technical. Because then, as always when you tackle fresh topics, you learn things. I, for example, learned that Manica – this firm that designs our stadium – has built six hundred stadiums around the world.

In a recent development, “They seized a great opportunity because opportunities like this are just the ones you get. And so I must say the negotiations concluded very successfully.”.

“We have all the authorisations in front of us by September 2027. Therefore, in principle, we could begin construction of the new stadium between the end of 2027 and the beginning of 2028. So, let’s say, we’re pretty close to the home stretch.

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 14:59 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 15:01 EST, 18 November 2026.

Bayern Munich's chief executive has confirmed Vincent Kompany is expected to return to the dugout on Friday, less than a month after collapsing at the club's training ground.

Kompany collapsed on October 23 while watching Bayern's Under-23 side and reportedly suffered from seizures.

The 40-year-old, who suffered a dislocated shoulder in the fall, underwent tests in hospital which determined that a 'meningeal irritation' had been the cause of his collapse.

According to recent reports, if left untreated meningeal irritation can become meningitis. The meninges are the membranes around the brain and spinal cord.

Kompany was discharged from hospital the following week to continue his recovery at home.

The Belgian coach is now set to return to the dugout when Bayern face Cologne on Friday, with Kompany due to also address the media tomorrow morning.

Vincent Kompany is set to return to the Bayern Munich dugout for their Bundesliga match on Friday.

Kompany's return was officially confirmed by Bayern chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen.

It has been revealed that 'Yes, Vincent is in pretty good spirits. I ran into him today,' Dreesen told German outlet Abendzeitung.

According to recent reports, 'The meningeal irritation has healed. He has already undergone shoulder surgery.'.

Kompany had led training for the first time since his collapse earlier this week, with his arm reportedly in a sling following his shoulder injury.

He had missed five matches during his recovery with Bayern winning two and drawing against Borussia Dortmund in the Bundesliga.

The German champions also beat Atletico Madrid in the Champions League in his absence, as well as progressing in the DFB Cup.

Kompany's assistant Aaron Danks had overseen the first team during his recovery.

Danks previously worked as Kompany's assistant at Anderlecht before deputising for Dean Smith and Steven Gerrard at Aston Villa and Michael Carrick at Middlesbrough.

Kompany has missed five matches following his collapse at Bayern's training ground on October 23.

Bayern had stressed they wanted to give Kompany as much time as required to recover before returning to work.

The German giants play eight matches in the next month, including two matches in the Champions League, before the Bundesliga takes its winter break.

Reports had emerged after Kompany's collapse that club officials had been concerned by his irregular eating habits, as well as barely exercising, drinking excessive amounts of coffee, and taking on too much work.

Bayern sporting director Max Eberl dismissed the claims last month, reiterating that Kompany's illness had been the cause of his collapse rather than his workload.

Mauricio Pochettino branded Manchester United "an amazing club" as the Argentine spoke to the media on Friday afternoon at his pre-Liverpool press conference.

Man United sacked Michael Carrick earlier this month before announcing that Pochettino had been appointed as his replacement.

The South American finished his duties with the USA before flying straight to England to begin work on Wednesday, with Man United back in action away to Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday afternoon.

Pochettino spoke to reporters at his pre-match press conference on Friday, and he detailed the importance of being ready for the clash with Liverpool.

"We are so excited to be here and I think it's an amazing club. We are happy, but at the same time, so busy. I think it's a race to arrive in condition to be competitive against Liverpool," said Pochettino.

"We arrive with the idea to create something from scratch, from our own ideas and philosophy with the way we love to work.

"We have found supportive people in the club. But at the same time, we need to improve our players and find a way to perform. The identity and the culture of the club are very clear; it's a historic club with years as one of the best in the world.

According to recent reports, "My first target is to sleep! But I cannot sleep, only three or four days a day. The target is to get to know the people, the staff, the players, and try to have an impact from the beginning, a positive one.

"We want to create something different and positive, to build our own way here. We feel the support from day one that we started to work. The most key thing is to think about the next action, not the past.".

Pochettino also confirmed that Bruno Fernandes would be remaining as captain of the 20-time English champions amid the speculation surrounding his future.

Fernandes had his issues this season, and it is understood that the Portugal international has rejected the chance to sign a new deal at Old Trafford.

However, Pochettino detailed the importance of the attacker during his press conference, and he is expected to be in the starting XI against Liverpool.

Industry observers note that "I think the commitment of all the players is amazing from day one. Bruno is our captain and he's a very notable player, but all the player must feel they are important. We chatted yesterday and spent three hours chatting in my office with all the players. I missed some injured players, but in the next few days, I will talk to everyone," he said.

The 32-year-old has scored six goals and registered three assists in 14 appearances for Man United during the 2026-27 campaign.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan have chosen the centre-forward they want in January, according to La Gazzetta dello Sport: Nicolo Tresoldi.

The newspaper write this morning that the ballot is settled, and there’s a winner: Milan have opted for Tresoldi as their attacking target in view of the winter. Part of the reason for this is because Endrick – the alternative name – made his intentions clear: “I hope to spend my life at Real Madrid.”.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Sources indicate that in this story of preferences, Tresoldi’s choice is also crucial. The 22-year-old has supported Milan since he was a child, while in Belgium and beyond he has proven himself to be a goal scorer. Inter found this out, as he scored a hat-trick against them in the Champions League at San Siro.

The No.9 shirt and role is currently occupied by Gonçalo Ramos, not a trivial thing due to the record-breaking fee paid for him last summer. However, Ruben Amorim genuinely believes the Portuguese can co-exist with Tresoldi, who can be on hand to finish the chances created by Ramos’ movement.

Recent findings suggest that tresoldi is a true ‘devil’ in the penalty area. He has 18 goals this season for club (eight in the league, five in the Champions League, and one in the Belgian Super Cup) and another four for Germany’s U21s. This leaves him just shy of 20 goals, in mid-November.

Tresoldi is also desperate to move to Milan and if it were up to him, the deal would be done. His desire to join his boyhood club could prove helpful and provide a boost to the deal’s success, just as it has before. His agents and family are equally positive about a potential Italian move.

Recent findings suggest that club Brugge are in a different mood, however, and would happily keep him unless offered at least €60m. Just a few months ago, the Belgian giants rejected offers just over half that. This is a figure Milan are willing to negotiate around, because Champions League qualification is crucial and goals are needed to achieve this.

Besides, Cardinale is of the opinion that it’s better to invest now than risk deepening the deficit. Another year without the revenues from the top club competition would be far from ideal for many different reasons.

What about Francesco Camarda? Here too, the debate is over: the club and the coach agree on the need for a loan, perhaps abroad. Camarda agrees: he knows he needs to regain rhythm by playing regularly, to help his development.

For Milan, it would be another negotiation with Brugge after Charles De Ketelaere and Ardon Jashari. The deal for the former was conducted by Paolo Maldini and Ricky Massara, while for the latter it was Igli Tare. Now, Cardinale intends to do things himself.

According to recent reports, the owner wants Tresoldi and is ready to sit at the table himself, while Nicolò remains ready to serve him a winning first pass. Milan want him in January, but if that weren’t possible, they would leave the discussion open for the summer.

Absolutely remarkable! Newcastle United 2 Arsenal 2

💡 Key Takeaways

  • If you ever wanted proof of how unpredictable football is, here is the ultimate proof.
  • They looked very much like they were the reigning champions and league leaders by five points.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Newcastle United 2 Arsenal 2 – Saturday 21 November 2026 5.30pm.

If you ever wanted proof of how unpredictable football is, here is the ultimate proof.

Arsenal absolutely dominated the first half.

They looked very much like they were the reigning champions and league leaders by five points.

Sources indicate that newcastle United didn’t get a kick. Well, not a kick where it mattered.

Arsenal dominating the ball and territory, Newcastle just clearing the ball and it coming straight back at them.

Bruno Guimaraes had headed a close in header just wide and it felt like a goal was inevitable.

It has been revealed that the visitors were breaking the half-hearted United press with ease and you really had to feel for Lewis Hall when the goal did come. He didn’t deal with a ball he should have, next thing Havertz with a very clever ball that Dedic wasn’t alive to and Eze giving Hornicek no chance.

Matthias Jaissle took decisive action for the second half, with Ramsey, Elanga and Livramento replacing Steur, Murphy and Dedic.

Inside four minutes Newcastle were level.

In almost the exact same part of the pitch, Odegaard made a far worse blunder than Hall had for their goal. Osula taking advantage to feed Barnes in the box and a great low finish.

It was then all suddenly Newcastle United pouring forward and the first half seemed like another match.

Just after the hour mark an excellent corner routine saw Hall cross from the right and Burn a free header, that caused chaos and Malick Thiaw on hand to smash it home from a yard out.

Var vainly tried to find a handball, then it was looking for an offside, before admitting defeat.

Somehow, somehow, Newcastle United were now ahead!

Newcastle didn’t sit back and continued to look for another goal, absolutely the right tactics. Rather than sit back.

Arteta making subs and Bruno Guimaraes trudging off as one of them.

The Arsenal equaliser was a great goal for them as they played it from back to front but Newcastle could have defended it better as Madueke cut inside. Plus Hornicek should have saved it, even though the shot went through a defender’s legs.

More than twenty minutes then played including nine minutes added time, with a pretty even closing period of the match, even though you naturally adopted the stance of you just know Arsenal are going to find a winner somehow….

This was absolutely remarkable stuff.

Never in a million years did you see that second half coming after Arsenal had total control of the first.

Newcastle at last seeing a bit of luck going their way with that Odegaard mistake and suddenly that helped give confidence and momentum. Plus it helped that United brought on three mobile players all able to carry the ball and with a bit of pace.

No doubt the extremist Matthias Jaissle haters won’t want to give him any credit.

However, I think he was brave with his substitutions and I have a feeling that whatever 11 he had played in the first half, we would have seen Arsenal dominate the opening 45.

A hopeless first half and a second half that gives hope.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 20 Nov 2026 14:21.

Enzo Maresca has provided the latest enhancement on the fitness of his Manchester City squad ahead of Saturday lunchtime’s Premier League clash at home to Fulham.

The Citizens enter this contest seeking to end a three-game losing run, with defeats to Aston Villa and Brighton & Hove Albion followed by a 3-1 loss at Nottingham Forest before the international break.

Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol both started at the City Ground and were at fault for goal conceded in the first half before coming off at half time due to injury.

While Gvardiol has since recovered from his minor issue and represented Croatia on international duty, Guehi withdrew from the England squad with a hip problem.

However, Guehi was involved in Man City training on Thursday and is set to be available for selection against Fulham.

Clarifying Guehi’s situation following a run of error-strewn performances before his injury, Maresca said at his press conference: “He didn't join internationally because he had a small problem against Forest, but it's not because he needs some break.”.

Fellow centre-back Abdukodir Khusanov pulled out of Uzbekistan duty after sustaining a knock in Man City’s defeat at Forest.

The 22-year-old was absent from all Man City photos and videos from Thursday’s training session and is now a doubt for the visit of Fulham this weekend.

Maresca has also confirmed that Matheus Nunes is a doubt with an unspecified issue; he previously missed three games in October with an ankle issue.

Sources indicate that "From the Forest game we still have Matheus (Nunes) and [Khusanov] that are still doubts for tomorrow, because they are still with some problems. We'll see in the next hours.".

The only confirmed injury absentee for Man City is attacker Antoine Semenyo, who is still recovering from a knee injury and is targeting a return next month.

Meanwhile, Maresca has confirmed one guaranteed starter for the match against Fulham, with goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma to continue between the sticks despite a poor run of form.

Donnarumma has kept just four clean sheets in 15 appearances across all competitions this season, conceding 23 goals in total, and his decision making in recent matches has come under question.

Industry observers note that however, Maresca continues to back his fellow Italian, telling reporters: "He has been good. I think with the international team, he made a mistake in the build-up, but for Italy he was the Man of the Match in the game (vs. France), he made many good saves.

"We made some mistakes in the last games. Gigi was part of that. He is aware. Hopefully he's not going to make any more mistakes. He is going to start against Fulham.".

Man City have kept just three clean sheets in their last nine meetings with Fulham, but they have won each of their last 20 head-to-head battles across all competitions – the longest winning run against the same opponent in English football history.

It has been revealed that west Ham’s veteran midfielder has been the subject of an honest interview in his home country on Czech radio coinciding with the release of his autobiography. One of the more revealing comments Tomas Soucek made concerns the pressure and the expectation of playing in front of a big audience – such as West Ham will undoubtedly face tomorrow as the season re-commences with a home tie at London Stadium in front of 60,000 expectant supporters.

Unlike several others, from his words it is clear that Soucek seems to thrive on the pressure and the weight of expectation upon him. As one of only a handful of medal winners still at the club from the 2023 campaign, Soucek’s experience should become a steadying influence in the dressing room even though he mostly starts games on the bench these days.

Handling the weight of expectation at London Stadium has been daunting at times.

‘Tornado Tom’ reveals that, far from letting it get to him, he actually enjoys the weight of expectation and pressure :.

“Yes, obviously I feel it, but I like the pressure. Because football is always up and down, you have so many wins and so many losses – and it’s up to you how you recover from all of it.

“And I love that. As you stated, it’s the most watched league in the world. And West Ham’s fans are crazy – they’re the best in the league, and it’s such a historic club.

“From the first day until now, I think me and West Ham connection is as good as it could possibly be in all aspects.

“And, yes, the pressure is there, but I try to work with it – and that’s why we play football.” (englishradio.cz).

Sources indicate that the pressure will be significantly eased with a clean sheet and three points tomorrow – whether Soucek now, 31 gets into the action or simply acts as a calming figure in the dressing room. He is one of those very rare characters in the West Ham team – a leader on and off the pitch – and in another era could have spent years as the club’s captain.

Instant fan/writer reaction from some of our regular contributors on The Mag.

‘I wouldn’t believe anyone if they claimed to have predicted that the second half would have been like that!

Have to mention the comeback of Tino, he’s top class along with our other England full back.

Captain’s performance as well tonight from Major Dan.

In the end a very well deserved point against the champions and current league leaders (could be greedy and say it could / should have been all three…).’.

‘Excellent second half after a first in which we looked low on confidence and bereft of ideas.

Fair play to Jaissle who had seen enough and his triple substitution paid dividends, United taking the game to Arsenal and unlucky not to have won.’.

‘Wow, terrible first half, brilliant second.

Atmosphere was flat considering the number one rat’s return but thanks to our players for finally realising that effort equals reward.’.

‘First half, woeful. Arsenal simply a class apart and it didn’t stick for any of our players.

Ultimately, we’d only earn a point despite being worthy of more with that second half performance.

Industry observers note that in a tough season, we’ve earned 5 points against our former star names. That’s a decent return. Please, please, please let us see that second half performance again soon.’.

‘Brilliant from Matthias Jaissle.

Every credit to him for making such decisive substitutions at the break.

We got a bit of luck with our equaliser via an Odegaard mistake (just like Arsenal did with their opening goal, mistake by Hall). ‘Some much much-needed signs of life as the champions are held on Bruno’s return to Tyneside.

Folklore denoting he was bound to get booed.

But on to the game and It was stirring to see us come back and turn the game on its head.

Sadly, it wasn’t quite enough for a win, yet we become the only side bar Brighton to get something off the Gunners so far this season.

Heading into this one I did wonder if a point would be considered a great outcome.

The players duly obliged amid some major talking points, not least the manager leaving £259m worth of signings on the bench, and a further £72m (Toure and Bamba) in the stands.

Result aside, I’m genuinely baffled.’.

‘That’s a point more than I thought we’d get.

And here’s another point to ponder.

How come every game we play in the first half after a week’s training and pre match instructions still fresh in their ears, we are awful?

And then when the players play the game in front of them in the second half they suddenly improve despite / regardless of the half time talk from the Head Coach?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 20 Nov 2026 14:27.

Tottenham Hotspur have shared footage of Lucas Bergvall and Savio back in training ahead of Saturday's Premier League clash with Ipswich Town.

The pair have both missed each of Spurs' last four Premier League matches, having picked up injuries ahead of October's 3-1 home victory over Coventry City.

Savio has been dealing with a muscular problem, while Bergvall has been nursing a knee injury, but Roberto De Zerbi expressed hope that the pair would return following the November international break.

On Friday, Spurs posted a 55-second clip on social media showing Savio and Bergvall in training with their teammates, taking part in warm-up exercises and drills with the ball at their feet.

Sávio and Bergvall in training ? ? @Betano_UK https://t.co/3Iug9LlBjf.

De Zerbi then confirmed at his pre-game press conference that the Brazilian attacker and Swedish midfielder are fine to feature against Ipswich, as well as assuring that James Maddison is fit and ready.

However, none of Mykhaylo Mudryk, Tosin Adarabioyo or Mathys Tel will be ready just yet, as the latter is still feeling the effects of the crunching tackle from Jayden Bogle in the 1-0 loss to Leeds United two weekends ago.

According to recent reports, "Bergvall, Maddison and Savio are back," De Zerbi stated. "Tosin and Mathys Tel no. Tosin is already okay but it is not the right moment to take any risks and Mathys Tel, we need another two or three weeks. Mudryk is not ready yet.".

With Tel sidelined for another two or three weeks, the Frenchman could miss each of Tottenham's next four matches, including the North London derby against Arsenal on December 6.

Opportunity knocks – if Piroe can extend his Preston scoring record tomorrow he could cement a place in the starting eleven for the rest of the year. 💡 Key Takeaways

  • Two football images adorn the walls of Martin Tyler’s latest home or at least they will when everything is in order.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MATT BARLOW, FOOTBALL WRITER.

Published: 13:55 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 15:04 EST, 18 November 2026.

Two football images adorn the walls of Martin Tyler’s latest home or at least they will when everything is in order.

Tyler has recently moved house and the large, framed photograph of Teddy Sheringham scoring for Nottingham Forest against Liverpool, the only goal of the first Premier League game broadcast live by Sky is still on the floor by the front door.

From wherever it ends up, it will project a moment in time when everything changed for Tyler, having walked away from a steady job at ITV and taken a leap of faith as lead commentator for the new satellite channel.

'A new frontier,' admits Tyler, the undisputed ‘Voice of the Premier League’ by the time he left the role at Sky, more than 30 years later.

'We didn’t know where it would take us, so that was a special day. Feeling a bit like a pioneer. Wondering whether we were all on a fool’s errand. Some people turned down the job I accepted because of the risk. My kids were four and two at the time.

According to recent reports, 'We used to travel to the games by train in those days, and we would look out of the window and count the satellite dishes as we passed through a big town. We didn’t know whether it was going to work. I wasn’t sure anybody would be watching.

Legendary football commentator Martin Tyler has released a book: TALES FROM THE GANTRY.

Tyler was the undoubted 'Voice of the Premier League' by the time he left Sky Sports in 2023.

In a recent development, 'It was slow off the ground and there was a feeling within the game against live football, that people wouldn’t go to the games if they were televised live, and it ended up the opposite. Attendances have gone up, an amazing paradox. Now you can’t get a ticket.'.

Televised football has come a long way since Tyler’s first commentary game, Southampton v Sheffield Wednesday in the old Division Two in 1974, shot with just four cameras for Southern Television.

'Now if you don’t have 24 cameras you can feel a bit short-changed,' he laughs. 'I worked at ITV for about 17 years, most of it commentating and you would get a crew on match day who had been doing Coronation Street or Emmerdale Farm in the week and a match director from light entertainment.'.

The Premier League has come a long way, too. Some might argue too far. It has led football from its roots as the working man’s game to a place where clubs are owned by nations states and mired in the legal complications of the Manchester City case.

Tyler wants to reserve comment on City’s financial offences until sentencing is passed, aware he is inextricably bound to their success because of his iconic commentary for Sergio Aguero’s winner in the 93rd minute against Queen’s Park Rangers to snatch the Premier League title from Manchester United in 2012.

'I’ve always stated you won’t see anything like it again, and I stick to that,' he says, although he the 'Aguero moment’ as it has become commonly known probably means less to him than it does to others.

He is proud to deliver the words but insists those moments belong to the players, the clubs and the fans, not to him.

Ask about his favourite game from three decades in the Premier League and Tyler instinctively pulls Liverpool’s 4-3 comeback win against Newcastle in 1996 from the thrillers he has called.

His own footballing background, meanwhile, could hardly be any further from the Premier League’s glitzy, moneyed elite.

Sources indicate that tyler has always supported Woking and played as an amateur for Corinthian-Casuals. 'The law was you couldn’t get paid,' he says. 'We were on expenses only and they weren’t dodgy expenses. If I went on the tube to Leytonstone, I got the tube fare repaid and no more.

In a recent development, 'I played for five years at that level and never got a penny because that was the rule. I played my last game in 1973 and within two years’ they got rid of it because so many people were bending the rules. An opposition player told me their team were on £75 a game.'.

Tyler reflected on his time in the game as a player, coach and commentator with Daily Mail Sport's Matt Barlow.

He was famously on commentary for Sergio Aguero's title-winning moment in 2012.

From a cricketing family, Tyler was on the books at Surrey where he twice served as 12th man and lived for a time with Bob Willis, who became one of England’s greatest fast bowlers after moving on to Warwickshire.

His manager for a time at Casuals was Surrey legend Micky Stewart, who had also played for the famous amateur football club before turning professional at Charlton. In those days it was possible for the multi-talented to hold down a decent career in two sports.

An afternoon in Tyler’s company is just as likely to involve digressions into non-league football, where he worked as an assistant to Alan Dowson at clubs including Woking and Hampton & Richmond, as it is into the Premier League.

He might regale you with a story about Arsene Wenger and the time, on the way to the gantry at Wigan Athletic, he slipped deeper than he realised into long conversation with the then Arsenal boss about rioting in Paris and almost missed his pre-match slot.

And he might pivot from there into Wenger’s fierce rivalry with Sir Alex Ferguson. 'I have seen Arsene very, very grumpy,' says Tyler. 'When he lost the FA Cup semi-final when Dennis Bergkamp missed the penalty and Ryan Giggs scored.

Industry observers note that 'I have never seen a manager so angry because he knew he had handed over not only an FA Cup final place but also the domination they enjoyed at that time. They had done the Double in 98 and he felt that was not only about losing a match but losing their psychological edge over their greatest rivals. He was livid. Talk about winning and losing with dignity.'.

But there’s every chance he will reminisce about the time when, as a schoolboy Woking supporter in the terrible winter of 1962-63 he was rewarded for volunteering to paint the stands with an invitation to travel on the team bus to an Amateur Cup tie at Lydbrook Athletic.

Industry observers note that 'We left Woking at seven on the morning of the match for a two o’clock kick-off in Gloucestershire and by nine we were digging the bus out of a snowdrift on the A4,' states Tyler. 'We got there at four, no floodlights, and they had marked the lines on the snow with blue soap powder but there was no way we could play. We turned around to go back, got stuck in Cheltenham and had to stay for the night.'.

The only other footballing image on display in Tyler’s home is a photograph of him and Dowson celebrating as the final whistle confirmed their Hampton & Richmond side as Isthmian League champions in 2016.

Tyler has had a hugely varied career, all the way from grassroots level right to the top.

Tyler even worked as an assistant coach to Alan Dowson at several Non-League clubs.

TALES FROM THE GANTRY: Letters from a Lifetime in Football by Martin Tyler is published by Pitch and out now HERE.

After collecting the trophy, Tyler jumped into his car, drove north and less than 24 hours later was at the King Power Stadium to see Leicester crowned champions of England.

It has been revealed that 'The greatest fairytale story in the Premier League,' as he claims. 'I had sampled that in a tiny non-league way, then taken those feelings with me to Leicester where it was multiplied a million times, but I could tell the world a tiny bit about how wonderful they must be feeling.'.

According to recent reports, the range of his experience is vast. From amateur football in the 60s, through regional television and ITV to Sky’s Premier League revolution. He commentates regularly and coaches at Woking’s academy and has written a book.

Recent findings suggest that it is a wonderful compilation of 110 essays, the reflections on his lifetime in football. 'The random thoughts of a football obsessive,' as he likes to call it.

TALES FROM THE GANTRY: Letters from a Lifetime in Football by Martin Tyler is published by Pitch and out now HERE.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, he needn’t have worried.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that andoni Iraola spun on his heels, turned his back to the action and began to bite his nails. Managers often envisage the worst outcome when the clock ticks down, and here, in the 93rd minute, Bournemouth had a corner.

In a recent development, he needn’t have worried. As the set-piece was swung in, Alisson Becker moved powerfully off his line and plucked the ball from the air, a catch that essentially confirmed Liverpool would leave Dorset with three points. It was a catch, too, that put the gloss on another impeccable personal afternoon.

Recent findings suggest that when Iraola took charge at Anfield, one question he had to answer – given Bournemouth had conceded 167 goals in his three years in charge – was whether he could make Liverpool defensively resilient. This dour 1-0 success, though, proves he is taking them in the right direction: he is the first Liverpool manager since Joe Fagan in 1983 to start with five unbeaten league games.

Alexander Isak might have scored the goal that leaves Bournemouth winless in the Premier League but this success owed everything to Alisson’s enduring brilliance – a comment that also applies to Virgil van Dijk – the enormous promise of Jérémy Jacquet and the grit of Ronaldo Araújo.

You go to top level football matches hoping to see something that will take your breath away and how Alisson did that in the 17th minute with a reflex save from an Evanilson backheel, the shape of his body resembling a fielder in the slips diving to prevent a boundary.

Industry observers note that it proved to be the foundation stone from which Liverpool were able to build and inflict Bournemouth’s first home defeat since January. There are plenty of [valid] questions to ask of Liverpool’s attack at present but, defensively, it is starting to come together.

In a recent development, “It was a really good fight,” Alisson mentioned, in that self-effacing way of his. “But we have to improve a lot – on the ball and sometimes off the ball as well but we improved in the second half. We adapted to the opponent and that’s what we are doing.”.

Recent findings suggest that any manager with a well-drilled defence stands a chance of improving and that is what Liverpool are doing. Only four weeks ago the discussion was about how easy it was for teams to play through their middle – remember that chaotic afternoon at Newcastle to start? – but that is changing swiftly.

Since Iraola replaced Jeremie Frimpong with Araújo at right-back, three consecutive Premier League clean sheets have followed. Araújo, the Uruguayan on loan from Barcelona, revels in doing the dirty work while Jacquet, the £60m signing from Rennes, oozes quality.

“He’s [Jacquet] very young and adapted really well to the Premier League,” Iraola said. “The first games, he was physically feeling the change of rhythm and I had to sub him. This was a step forward. He looked solid until the end. He’s in a good place physically and I hope he can continue his development.”.

Industry observers note that don’t confuse positivity about one aspect of the team as being a guide to its collective health. There was always a chance this contest would become a cagey affair and, Evanilson’s chance aside, the opening 45 minutes were as flat as you could imagine.

Iraola again played his three £100m+ signings but Bradley Barcola is still adjusting to the physicality of English football and Florian Wirtz is still finding it difficult to impose himself on a game; patience with the German will not be infinite.

He would do worse than to look at Isak, who is now on a run of four goals in four league games and is influencing games in the manner Liverpool envisaged when they broke the British transfer record to sign him last August.

It has been revealed that isak had an unusual afternoon. His only shot in the first half almost took out some low-flying pigeons, a cross early in the second half was sliced so badly that the weekend hackers on the nearby Queens Park golf course would have felt a flood of sympathy but then he got his third opening.

Sources indicate that cody Gakpo, who could have been in Manchester City blue had the cards played out differently earlier this month, wriggled down the right flank and squeezed in a cross that Isak seized upon and turned in from six yards. Liverpool never looked back.

Sources indicate that alexander Isak grabs his fourth Premier League goal of the season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/5ehwhl1it4.

“A striker’s job is like this,” Iraola remarked, who badgered Isak persistently to press Bournemouth’s defence. “He had a couple of crosses that he did not hit properly or control. He has to help us to be closer to the box, to play in the opposition’s half and have more meaningful possession. And then if the team is playing there, he will receive rewards in terms of goals.”.

In a recent development, one, ultimately, was enough to see off Bournemouth, whose start to the campaign is something of a riddle. They shouldn’t be anywhere near the relegation places but that is the reality and Thursday’s historic Europa League win in Real Sociedad couldn’t mask the home crowd’s frustration.

Sources indicate that “Our attitude and effort is good,” head coach Marco Rose said. “But, at this level, small things and little details decide games.”.

According to recent reports, speaking to Sky Sports after the match, Iraola stated: “I’m obviously happy with the result because I know this is a difficult place to come, very difficult place to get three points. And we could see it, especially in the beginning of the game. In the first 20 minutes we weren’t at the level [required] and it cost us. We finished the first half better and in the second half we played better, but that beginning of the game has surprised us, not surprised us [because] we knew where we were coming but it [was] difficult for us.”.

It has been revealed that jeremy Jacquet has made the kind of quietly authoritative start to his Liverpool career that showed why there was such excitement in February within the club when they completed his deal. Sources indicate that andoni Iraola returns to Bournemouth this weekend knowing what to expect from players he understands so well. Sadly, I do not mean Liverpool’s.

Having built his reputation creating a hard-working, well-drilled team rich in potential, Iraola is responsible for infusing those same characteristics into the most expensively assembled squad in Liverpool history.

His first six games demonstrate it is no quick fix. The Basque coach is the first Liverpool appointment to work with more than £700m of recent signings while being entitled to feel he has been dealt a bad hand.

Everything Iraola has said and done so far screams that he is searching for the right blend in his starting XI while having to eradicate negative traits, with and without the ball. It was telling that the excellent performance of his youngsters against Tottenham Hotspur in midweek offered the clearest hint of Iraola’s vision than anything we have seen with all the high-priced stars on the pitch.

In a recent development, there is a reason the Kop stood to acclaim the energy and application of youngsters Lewis Koumas, James McConnell and Trey Nyoni – and why Iraola keeps name-checking them. Iraola is indebted to them for issuing a reminder of the non-negotiables that come with being a Liverpool footballer; regardless of price tag and reputation, leaving everything on the pitch is compulsory. It is a concern that so many of the renowned players need to hear that message.

Jurgen Klopp named Florian Wirtz in his first squad as Germany manager and has remarked that fans must refrain from expecting “special moments” from the Liverpool playmaker as a matter of course.

Of Wirtz, he remarked: “I think he’s the player who covered the most ground at Liverpool this season, so the willingness is absolutely there.

“We have to move away from the idea that we need to see special moments from him. He is there to help us as a team. We have to make sure that Flo feels comfortable with us.”.

Wirtz has delivered seven goals and 11 assists in his 54 Liverpool appearances.

Adam Smith, 35, played for Iraola 81 times and he admitted his former manager’s visit to the Vitality will be a sentimental affair. He mentioned: “It’s going to be an emotional day for everyone I think, [for] our ex-manager and some of our players that have played under him, but we’ll be up for the game for sure.”.

Truffert topped the charts for most overlapping runs by any player in Europe’s top five leagues last season and laid on five assists.

Speaking before his return to the South Coast, Iraola noted: “I know where we are going [the Vitality], and I know the stats they have there [unbeaten in 12 matches], not only in their stadium, overall, I think if you see the games they’ve lost in a long while, you realise how difficult it is to beat Bournemouth.

“But, I suppose I also have the advantage that I know them very well, they also have the advantage that they know me very well, so you never know who has more advantage in that sense.

In a recent development, he added: “On a personal side, I’m very much looking forward to meet them [his former players], to hug them. It’s players that I love, staff that I’ve been working with who I appreciate so much, and I was pushing for them [against Real Sociedad] when they were playing their first European game. I wish them all the best, but there is another part, which is the most crucial one right now that we need to go there and win.”.

Recent findings suggest that good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League match between Liverpool and Bournemouth as Andoni Iraola returns to the Vitality Stadium for the first time since his major move up north. The Basque propelled Bournemouth to latest heights, guiding the club into Europe and his successor, Marco Rose, ensured they made a winning start to life on the Continent by defeating Real Sociedad in midweek.

Previewing Iraola’s Vitality Stadium return, Craig Beazley, host and creator of the Up The Cherries In All Departments podcast, noted: “We’ve now got the Andoni Iraola return … Andoni is very much a legend really, there should be a statue of Sir Eddie Howe and Sir Andoni Iraola [outside the ground] as well.”.

Across three seasons, Iraola guided Bournemouth to 12th, ninth and sixth in the Premier League, winning 47 of his 127 matches in charge (37 per cent).

Liverpool are still acclimatising to his exacting style of play and their results suggest as much. They are 10th in the table having drawn three and won one, impressing in flashes but struggling to maintain consistently productive final-third patterns and pressing structures. Deploying Ronald Araújo at right-back has proved effective, though, with Liverpool conceding just two goals in their last four matches.

According to recent reports, the Cherries are searching for their first Premier League win of the season and have retained the 4-2-3-1 shape from the Iraola days, with Rose preferring a similarly vertical attacking strategy. They continue to leverage their strengths in transitions and in wide areas as Adrien Truffert rains in crosses for any one of Bournemouth’s exuberant frontline to pounce on.

Elsewhere, Manchester City welcome Sunderland, who also secured a Europa League win during the week, to the Etihad while in-form Leeds United host Crystal Palace knowing a win would lift them into the top four.

Match day morning : Here’s what West Ham fans need today – and it is more than just ‘hope’

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (331 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Claretandhugh

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There have been two weeks of no football and only fine words by which to judge Scott Parker’s fresh era at West Ham.
  • This is the first game in which Parker’s work to date will be judged by West Ham’s home supporters.
  • Fans have ‘upcoming manager fatigue’ – if there is such a thing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There have been two weeks of no football and only fine words by which to judge Scott Parker’s fresh era at West Ham. Well received, the new manager has expressed himself eloquently in terms that supporters will love. However, this is the fifth manager in three years to come through the doors at London Stadium and each one has spoken with well-judged words.

This is the first game in which Parker’s work to date will be judged by West Ham’s home supporters.

Tottenham Hotspur are reportedly interested in signing Inter Milan midfielder Hakan Calhanoglu.

After enjoying a memorable spell at AC Milan, Calhanoglu switched to their cross-city rivals Inter in the summer of 2021 and has since made 225 appearances across all competitions.

The highly-skilled central midfielder has scored 53 goals and registered 39 assists for Inter, while continuing to impress with his performances this season.

However, his contract situation has cast doubt over his long-term future at the club, with several sides, including Tottenham, reportedly looking to take advantage of the uncertainty.

The Turkish international has a contract at San Siro until 2027, but he is yet to receive an offer to extend his stay.

The 32-year-old wants to continue with Inter, although doing so could require him to accept a significant pay cut, something he is right now unwilling to consider.

According to TuttoMercatoWeb, Tottenham are ready to welcome the midfielder, but face competition from Galatasaray, Juventus and Como.

Spurs spent heavily during the summer transfer window to overhaul their midfield, bringing in Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes on massive-money deals.

After a nightmare start to the season, Roberto De Zerbi's side are gradually climbing the table and at the moment sit 11th in the Premier League table with 12 points from 10 matches.

De Zerbi already has plenty of midfield options at his disposal, but it appears he wants a technically gifted and versatile player with proven experience, making Calhanoglu an attractive option.

Calhanoglu operates primarily as a defensive midfielder, although his creative qualities remain a significant asset.

Furthermore, the former Bayer Leverkusen midfielder is renowned for his excellent long-range shooting and could adapt well to the Premier League, even at this stage of his career.

Noni Madueke was Arsenal’s star player against Newcastle United at St James’ Park.

I think it is the best I have seen him play for either England or Arsenal.

Eze gave the visitors a 33rd minute lead and it could have been even worse for the hosts as Arsenal were by far the better side in the first half.

We then saw one of those remarkable turnarounds that make football so special and bizarre, Matthias Jaissle making three subs at the break and when Barnes equalised it then saw Newcastle by a distance the better team in the second 45.

Malick Thiaw putting United ahead from a corner routine before a great run and goal from Noni Madueke saw the game finish 2-2, although Lukas Hornicek should probably have saved it even though the ball went through a defender’s legs.

Noni Madueke very honest when reflecting on the match: “A game of two halves is fair. I thought we were outstanding in the first half and should have gone in with a minimum three-goal lead. Then the second half we weren’t at our standard in the first 20 minutes and when you give this crowd and team belief, it’s difficult. In the end I think 2-2 is a fair result.”.

Noni Madueke adding: “You know what to expect from Newcastle at home. The first 20 minutes of the second half is us not sticking by our own principles. I don’t know if we were too relaxed after our first-half performance.”.

Noni Madueke on his goal and performance: “The manager has been on me about being ahead of the game, I gambled and tried to stay onside. When I got the ball with that space I knew I had to score. I feel good. There are still things I can improve on but I feel trust from my coach and team-mates.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It was a game of varying fortunes for Lewis Hall against Arsenal.

In a first half when Newcastle United struggled to even get out of their own half, the England left-back was one of the very few prepared to take responsibility and try to keep the ball, even when under pressure.

Sources indicate that when dealing with a difficult ball and facing his own goal just after the half hour mark, Lewis Hall attempted to get the ball down and keep possession. It backfired though with Kai Havertz stealing possession and played in Eze for the opening goal.

Like the rest of the team, a far better second half from Lewis Hall.

Especially as with Newcastle United pressing higher as a team AND doing it well, it allowed Hall to play a lot more in the opposition half and use his attacking skills on the ball to great effect.

Just as an absorbing game had gone into the nine minutes of added time, Lewis Hall was left limping after he had blocked a cross and having tried to carry on, was then having to limp off a minute or so later and be replaced by Sven Botman.

Following the match, Matthias Jaissle asked whether Lewis Hall was now an injury worry: “Hopefully it is only just a cramp that meant Lewis Hall had to come off. That is what we are hoping.”.

It has been revealed that lewis Hall, along with others, had put so much into this match, it could well have been cramp. I know when I played football (at a lowly level!), towards the end of the match that can easily happen, you are fatigued and then when you are stretching the blocking of a cross/pass can impact you painfully and set off a cramp. Here’s hoping.

Matthias Jaissle also asked about his other England full-back.

Tino Livarmento had only managed 33 Premier League minutes this season as once again impacted by injuries, in that second half though we were reminded just how good he can be, both in defence and attack.

Matthias Jaissle: “Tino can definitely give us another dimension to our play but we also have to be careful and smart. He was really on the limit of what he could do. I was really proud that he could deliver 45 minutes with that physicality in such an intense match. It was really well played, a top performance, and also something that he can build on.”.
