a, Characteristics of the two studies. b, Test–retest ICC(2,1) for bilateral, left and right regional volumes (two-way random-effects, absolute agreement, single measurement). Points are ICC estimates. Bars show 95% confidence intervals computed by irr::icc. n = 8 independent participants, each scanned twice (16 scans, paired measurements). Red indicates ICC < 0.4. c, Pearson correlation heatmap of hypothalamic structure volumes and age at MRI in cognitively normal, amyloid-negative participants (n = 165 independent participants). Blue and red indicate positive and negative correlations, respectively. Two-sided Pearson tests used Benjamini–Hochberg (BH) correction across all pairwise correlations (*adjusted P < 0.05, **adjusted P < 0.01, ***adjusted P < 0.001). d, Age–volume Pearson r in cognitively normal, amyloid-negative participants, analysed as pooled (black, n = 165), CBA (orange, n = 91) and AMBR (blue, n = 74) samples. Two-sided Pearson tests used BH correction across 26 age–volume correlations per analysis. Filled circles indicate adjusted P < 0.05, open circles non-significance. e, Associations of age, female sex and intracranial volume with subregion volumes in AMBR, CBA and pooled participants. Points show Gaussian GLM coefficients. Bars show unadjusted approximate 95% confidence intervals (estimate ± 1.96 × s.e.). Every regional model used 107 AMBR, 209 CBA or 316 pooled independent participants. Models included age, sex, cognition, amyloid-β, cognition × amyloid-β and intracranial volume, plus study in pooled models. Two-sided t-tests used 100, 202 and 308 residual degrees of freedom, respectively. BH correction covered 26 regions per predictor and cohort. Exact estimates, intervals, t statistics, degrees of freedom and raw/adjusted P are in Supplementary Tables 2–4. In the figure panels, AN denotes the arcuate nucleus (ARC in the main text) and DM denotes the dorsomedial hypothalamic nucleus (DMH in the main text).

a, Pearson correlation heatmap of extrahypothalamic volumes and age at MRI (n = 458 independent participants). Blue and red indicate positive and negative correlations, respectively. Two-sided Pearson tests used Benjamini–Hochberg (BH) correction across unique pairwise correlations within the matrix (*adjusted P < 0.05, **adjusted P < 0.01, ***adjusted P < 0.001). b, Age–volume Pearson correlations in the pooled cohort (n = 458 independent participants), CBA (n = 256) and AMBR (n = 202). Two-sided Pearson tests used BH correction across all 26 regional age–volume correlations within each cohort. Filled circles indicate adjusted P < 0.05. Open circles indicate adjusted P ≥ 0.05. c, Forest plots of Gaussian GLM coefficients for hypothalamic (top) and extrahypothalamic (bottom) volumes, ordered by coefficient estimate. Points show fitted coefficients and bars show unadjusted approximate 95% confidence intervals (estimate ± 1.96 × SE). n = 316 independent participants in every model, with covariates as in Fig. 1c. Two-sided coefficient t-tests used 308 residual degrees of freedom. BH adjustment covered all eight coefficients, including the intercept, within each regional model. Point color and size indicate adjusted significance. d, Age, female sex and intracranial volume coefficients for extrahypothalamic structures. Points show Gaussian GLM coefficients and bars show unadjusted approximate 95% confidence intervals (estimate ± 1.96 × SE). Every regional model used 107 AMBR, 209 CBA or 316 pooled independent participants. Models included age, sex, cognition, amyloid-β, cognition × amyloid-β and intracranial volume, plus study in the pooled analysis. Two-sided coefficient t-tests used 100, 202 and 308 residual degrees of freedom, respectively. P values were BH-adjusted across 26 regions separately for each predictor and cohort. e, Body mass index (BMI) associations in AMBR-only Gaussian GLMs. Points show BMI coefficients per SD of BMI and bars show unadjusted approximate 95% confidence intervals (estimate ± 1.96 × SE). n = 174 independent participants in each regional model. Models adjusted for age, sex, cognition, amyloid status, cognition × amyloid status, HbA1c, Epworth sleepiness score and intracranial volume. Two-sided coefficient t-tests used 164 residual degrees of freedom. BH adjustment covered all ten model coefficients, including the intercept, within each regional model. Exact results for all panels are in Supplementary Tables 2–4. In the figure panels, AN denotes the arcuate nucleus (ARC in the main text) and DM denotes the dorsomedial hypothalamic nucleus (DMH in the main text).

Sources indicate that a, PCA of 25 hypothalamic and extrahypothalamic structure volumes (n = 458 participants). Scatter plots are colored by eight covariates: age, sex, amyloid-β status, cognitive status, intracranial volume (ICV), total brain volume (TBV), study and amyloid days. Three variants are shown: raw volumes (top, PC1 = 44.2%, PC2 = 14.4%), fully residualized for age, sex, ICV, TBV and study (middle, PC1 = 27.6%, PC2 = 13.1%), and partially residualized for sex, ICV, TBV and study (bottom, PC1 = 27.4%, PC2 = 13.9%). b–c, PC1 and PC2 loadings from raw (b) and fully residualized (c) PCA. Bars are red for negative loadings and teal for positive loadings. d, Changes in PC1 (left) and PC2 (right) loadings from raw (orange) to fully residualized (green) PCA, shown as dumbbell plots ordered by magnitude of change. e, Associations of PC1–PC5 scores with nine covariates in raw and partially residualized PCA. Continuous covariates were tested using two-sided Pearson correlations, with r2 as effect size. Categorical covariates were tested using omnibus one-way ANOVA F-tests, with η2 as effect size and an upper-tail F reference distribution. P values were Benjamini–Hochberg (BH)-adjusted across 45 PC–covariate tests separately for each PCA variant. n = 458 participants, with data available for cognitive status in 422, amyloid-β status in 340, CogDays in 441 and AmyloidDays in 358. *Adjusted P < 0.05, **adjusted P < 0.01, ***adjusted P < 0.001. f, Regional volume versus age in n = 181 independent male participants. Each point represents one participant, colored by combined cognitive and amyloid status (black, missing status). Black LOESS curves estimate conditional mean volume. Shading indicates pointwise 95% confidence intervals for the fitted curves, rather than between-participant standard deviations. g, Regional volume distributions after nearest-neighbor propensity-score matching of AD and cognitively unimpaired, amyloid-negative participants on sex and age. The pooled comparison includes 24 AD participants (18 men, 6 women) and 24 matched controls (16 men, 8 women). Center lines show medians, box bounds the 25th and 75th percentiles, and whiskers the most extreme observations within 1.5 × the interquartile range of the box bounds. Dots represent individual participants, including observations beyond the whiskers. Duplicate outlier symbols are suppressed. h, ROC curves from class-balanced logistic regression with five-fold stratified cross-validation, using 13 hypothalamic subregion volumes or total hypothalamic volume to predict cognitive impairment (n = 422 participants, 140 impaired, 282 unimpaired), amyloid positivity (n = 340, 63 positive, 277 negative) and AD status (n = 316, 24 AD, 292 others). AUCs are mean ± standard deviation across five folds. The subregion model had a higher mean AUC for all three outcomes. No formal comparison was performed. i, Univariate ROC curves predicting AD status from 25 hypothalamic and extrahypothalamic structures and total hypothalamic volume (n = 316 participants, 24 AD, 292 others), sorted by descending AUC. The arcuate nucleus (AN; ARC in the main text), fornix (fx), paraventricular nucleus (Pa) and ventromedial nucleus (VM) were the strongest predictors. When lower volume predicted AD (indicated by “−”), scores were sign-inverted before ROC calculation.

a, Donor metadata. The table summarizes condition, age, Braak stage, APOE genotype, amyloid-β status, postmortem delay (PMD), RNA integrity number (RIN) and time of death for each donor. Accompanying heatmaps show donors clustered by pathology metrics (left) and quality metrics (right), with annotation bars indicating condition, time of death, pathology and quality. b, UMAP showing nuclei from this study embedded within a reference atlas of 25 million publicly available human brain cells, colored by major cell type and condition. c, UMAP of the integrated dataset following scVI batch correction, with nuclei colored by condition, batch, individual, and inclusion of the Siletti et al. dataset. d, Boxplots of the per-tissue-sample mean number of genes detected per nucleus, stratified by cell type and condition. Each tissue sample is one hypothalamic subregion from one donor. The center line is the median, box bounds are the 25th and 75th percentiles, and whiskers extend to the most extreme observations within 1.5 × the interquartile range of the box bounds. Observations beyond the whiskers are shown as points. CTL and AD contain seven donors each (AD includes the familial case). Young reference samples derive from three donors, except young epithelial cells, which derive from one donor. In cell-type order neuron, epithelial, endothelial, ependymal, OPC, astrocyte, fibroblast, oligodendrocyte, microglia, and leukocyte, n (CTL/AD/young tissue samples) is 21/21/24, 8/4/2, 21/21/19, 19/17/19, 21/21/24, 21/21/24, 21/21/23, 21/21/24, 21/21/22 and 21/21/19. The epithelial samples come from four CTL and three AD donors. These are descriptive summaries, and no inferential test is shown. e, Boxplots of the per-tissue-sample mean UMI count per nucleus, with the same samples and group sizes as d. Boxplot elements are as in d. The y-axis is logarithmic. No inferential comparison is presented. f, Stacked bar plots showing cell-type composition for samples from each hypothalamic subregion (SCN, MN, and ARC). g, Bar plot quantifying the total number of nuclei for each cell type in the final dataset.

Selected significantly enriched Hallmark (top) and Gene Ontology biological process (GO:BP; bottom) pathways from GSEA. The analysis was performed on genes ranked by their signed model weights. The dot plot highlights the top pathways for the all-cell model and for each of the five cell-type-specific models. The x-axis represents the absolute NES, dot size represents the number of genes in a pathway, and color indicates significance (−log10[FDR]).

It has been revealed that a, Top row: violin plots displaying significant DEGs across specific major cell types (endothelial cells, microglia, and OPCs) from snRNA-seq, comparing CTL and AD individuals. Bottom row: boxplots illustrating the normalized log2 abundance of the corresponding significant differentially abundant proteins (DAPs) in CSF, comparing healthy controls (HC) with AD patients. Statistical significance with BH correction is indicated by asterisks (*P < 0.05, **P < 0.01, ***P < 0.001, ****P < 0.0001). b, UMAP projections illustrating the expression scores for three senescence-related and three NFT-related gene signatures across all nuclei. c, Violin plots comparing the expression scores of three NFT-related signatures across major cell types. Per-sample mean UCell scores for the NFT Orr signature were higher in AD than control (Wilcoxon rank-sum test on 18 AD versus 21 control samples, BH-adjusted across cell types: microglia P = 0.037, OPC P = 0.025). d, Violin plots showing the expression of key senescence-related genes (CDKN1A, canonical; CALR, responses; SOD2, initiators) across major cell types. Pseudobulk edgeR-LRT false discovery rate (FDR) is indicated by asterisks (*P < 0.05, **P < 0.01, ***P < 0.001, ****P < 0.0001). e–f, Module scores for the mTOR signaling (e) and extracellular matrix (ECM; f) gene sets, comparing control and AD donors at the sample level, stratified by cell type. Scores were computed using Seurat’s AddModuleScore (background-corrected mean expression relative to randomly sampled control gene sets matched by expression level). Each point represents the mean per-sample score for a given cell type (minimum 10 cells per sample). Boxes show median and IQR; whiskers extend to 1.5 × IQR. Brackets indicate pairwise comparisons with BH-adjusted significance (Wilcoxon rank-sum test).

a, Split UMAP embeddings of hypothalamic microglia/macrophage nuclei by group: young, 3,213 nuclei (3 donors), CTL, 24,648 (7 donors), AD, 20,087 (6 donors), and AD_44, 3,472 (1 donor), totaling 51,420 nuclei. In each panel, the full population is shown in light gray and the indicated group is overlaid, colored by inferred pseudotime (top), group identity (middle) or local nuclear density (2D kernel density estimate, bottom). Young nuclei occupy a discrete low-pseudotime region, whereas AD nuclei are shifted toward high pseudotime. b, Group-specific kernel density estimates of pseudotime, with the pooled distribution shown in gray. Nucleus and donor counts are as in a. Dashed vertical lines mark mean pseudotime: young 1.50, CTL 2.38, AD 2.90 and AD_44 2.12. The distribution shifts rightward from young to CTL to AD. c, Empirical cumulative distributions of nuclear pseudotime. The maximal vertical separation between AD and CTL is the Kolmogorov–Smirnov distance D = 0.27, presented as a descriptive effect size. Because nuclei within a donor are not independent, inference used donor-level mean pseudotime: AD versus CTL, 6 versus 7 donors, two-sided exact Wilcoxon rank-sum test, P = 0.0047. Young and AD_44 are shown descriptively and were not tested. d, Group composition of 22 fixed-width pseudotime bins (width 0.2, early to late from left to right). Each bar shows the fraction of nuclei contributed by each group. Nucleus and donor counts are as in a. Young and AD_44 were shown descriptively and were not tested. The AD fraction increases along pseudotime (Spearman ρ = 0.97, n = 22 bins, two-sided unadjusted P = 1.0 × 10−13), from near-absence in the earliest bins to dominance in the latest bins. A donor-aware binomial mixed model (in-segment versus out, group + (1 | donor), two-sided Wald tests, BH-adjusted across 44 segment × comparison tests) demonstrated AD nuclei were underrepresented relative to CTL in early bins 4–9 (log-OR − 3.23 to −1.28, adjusted P ≤ 0.017) and overrepresented in late bins 16–21 (log-OR +0.62 to +1.31, adjusted P ≤ 0.044), with a single crossover at pseudotime ≈ 2.3–2.9. Exact estimates for every bin are in Supplementary Table 10. e, Nuclear pseudotime by group, with counts as in a. Center lines show medians, box bounds the 25th and 75th percentiles, and whiskers the most extreme observations within 1.5 × the interquartile range. Nuclei beyond the whiskers are plotted individually. This panel is descriptive. See c for donor-level inference. f, Top: per-nucleus expression of CSF1R, APOE, B2M and TIMP2 in microglia (same data as Fig. 4f). Violin widths show nuclear density. Embedded boxes show medians and 25th–75th percentiles, with whiskers extending to the most extreme observations within 1.5 × the interquartile range. Outliers are not drawn separately. Asterisks indicate FDRs from pseudobulk edgeR likelihood-ratio tests (AD versus CTL, 1 d.f., one pseudobulk per sample, 18 AD samples from 6 donors and 21 CTL samples from 7 donors, BH-adjusted across genes): CSF1R FDR = 3.1 × 10−7 (****). APOE, B2M and TIMP2 were nonsignificant (FDR ≥ 0.05). Young and AD_44 were shown descriptively and excluded from these tests. Bottom: CSF protein abundance in young healthy controls (<65 years, n = 38 participants), aged healthy controls (≥65 years, n = 167) and AD (n = 19). Center lines show medians, box bounds the 25th and 75th percentiles, and whiskers the most extreme observations within 1.5 × the interquartile range. Each dot represents one participant. g, Embeddings of microglial trajectory-associated genes, colored by trajectory rank (left) or correlation with AD status (right).

It has been revealed that a, Concordance of AD-associated log2 fold changes between HypoAD (x-axis) and PsychAD dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (y-axis) for genes significant in both datasets (FDR < 0.05). Juventus vs Venezia - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (671 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Jonathan O'Shea | 20 Nov 2026 15:24, Last updated: 22 Nov 2026 09:23.
  • Set to clash in Serie A's Sunday lunchtime slot, fallen giants Juventus and promoted strugglers Venezia will meet in Turin this weekend.
  • Having limped into the international break, Juve at the moment trail Italy's top six, while their Venetian visitors are stuck inside the drop zone despite finally posting a second win of the season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 20 Nov 2026 15:24, Last updated: 22 Nov 2026 09:23.

Set to clash in Serie A's Sunday lunchtime slot, fallen giants Juventus and promoted strugglers Venezia will meet in Turin this weekend.

Having limped into the international break, Juve at the moment trail Italy's top six, while their Venetian visitors are stuck inside the drop zone despite finally posting a second win of the season.

Though Juventus are on track to reach the Europa League's knockout phase without needing a playoff, domestic results have been below par for several months.

After missing out on Champions League qualification at the bitter end of last season, the Bianconeri sit seventh in Serie A and are lacking the consistency required to mount a title charge.

Remarkably, Juve have gone 10 league games without consecutively recording the same result, and they signed off for the international break with a run of one defeat, one win and one draw.

Having lost 2-0 to Genoa, before beating Napoli by the same scoreline in Turin, Luciano Spalletti's side had to fight back twice to salvage a 2-2 draw with Fiorentina last time out.

Ahead of Thursday's Europa League game and next week's clash with high-flying Como, they must avoid another slip-up when Venezia come to town.

A former coach of Sunday's visitors, Spalletti is under heavy pressure, and he will only be able to celebrate his 600th Serie A match as a manager if Juventus claim maximum points.

History suggests that the hosts should prevail, as Venezia have lost 11 of their 14 top-flight away games against Juve, while drawing the other three.

In fact, the Lagunari's last victory against the Bianconeri anywhere dates back to a home success in April 1962.

This time, they will head to Turin under survival specialist Davide Nicola, who recently replaced promotion-winning boss Giovanni Stroppa.

Though Nicola's fresh side impressively upset Napoli in his first match, they subsequently lost three times without scoring, ahead of a big relegation six-pointer against Udinese.

Sending Stadio Penzo into raptures, Kike Perez scored a stunning goal that separated the pair in a tense 2-1 home win for Venezia, lifting them above their hapless visitors and off the foot of the table.

However, the Arancioneroverdi have yet to pick up any points on the road, while Nicola has previously suffered seven straight defeats in his managerial head-to-head with Spalletti.

Juventus form (all competitions):.

Though Juventus still have a long injury list, utility men Zeki Celik and Andrea Cambiaso have returned to full training and are both in contention to start.

Francisco Conceicao is also back in the fold, but Kenan Yildiz, Khephren Thuram, Pierre Kalulu, Kamil Grabara, Nico Gonzalez and captain Manuel Locatelli are all unavailable.

Set to start up front, Nick Woltemade finally scored his first Serie A goal against Fiorentina; like strike partner Randal Kolo Muani, he has fared better in this season's Europa League.

After posting three goal involvements from his last two matches, Kolo Muani will hope to continue that form this weekend.

Meanwhile, French wing-back Antoine Hainaut and Nigeria striker Akor Adams are Venezia's joint-top scorers with just two league goals, and the Lagunari have Serie A's lowest shot conversion rate (5.4%).

Either Lion Lauerbach or John Yeboah should partner Adams, the visitors' club-record signing.

Fellow forward Andrea Adorante returned from a layoff during the break, but Marin Sverko and Bartol Franjic are still sidelined. Toma Basic and Pasquale Mazzocchi will also miss out through injury.

Juventus possible starting lineup:.

Vicario; Celik, Bremer, Lucumi; McKennie, Luiz, Koopmeiners, Cabal; Kolo Muani, Alajbegovic; Woltemade.

Venezia possible starting lineup:.

Stankovic; Halhal, Moreno, Jesus; Hainaut, Perez, Busio, Sohm, Haps; Yeboah, Adams.

The pressure is all on Juventus, who have consistently frittered away points with weak defending and wayward finishing.

Even so, the hosts should have too much nous and skill for a Venezia side that face an improbable fight for survival.

Akram Jadid’s name has been in the headlines again recently, and for good reason given his exploits on international duty.

Calciomercato.com begin a report by stating that Ruben Amorim had already made a note of Jadid’s qualities, given that he called him up to first team training at the end of August, just days before the win against Venezia.

Industry observers note that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In a recent development, the coach has been ‘bewitched’ by the young talent, and it was a first opportunity for the teenager to work with the senior side. The staff also got to see exactly what level he is at, given that his scoring record gave him a reputation after netting over 700 goals in the lower levels.

Jadid represents another diamond in the youth sector for Milan, one that needs to be nurtured in the best possible way. Having risen up the age groups, he is currently a key player in Vito Michele Antonelli’s U18 team.

According to recent reports, last season, he was a key figure in the U15’s Scudetto victory, thanks in part to his goal in the final against Empoli. The fact he has been promoted multiple levels since indicates a lot about how he is through of internally.

The report described Jadid as ‘a lively, mobile left winger who enjoys constantly taking on opponents to create numerical superiority and finish, or pass (depending on the situation). He is a No.10 for his technical ability and vision, and a No.9 in the penalty area for his eye for goal’.

According to recent reports, in this first part of the season, Jadid has made eight appearances – all as a starter – and has scored four goals against Atalanta, Inter and Lecce. He continued this good form for his country with a hat-trick for Morocco U17s in the Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers victory over Tunisia.

🇲🇦 #ACMilan youth star Akram Jadid scored a hat-trick inside five minutes for Morocco U17s ⭐️⚽⚽⚽.

— SempreMilan (@SempreMilanCom) November 17, 2026.

He scored three times in five minutes. The third goal was particularly impressive: after anticipating the opposing defender and pounced on a loose ball, Jadid moved inside, evaded the return of another opponent, and concluded his solo effort with a curling right-footed shot that left the goalkeeper with no chance.

What comes next? For now, Akram Jadid will continue to grow with the U18 side, but the plan is that in the coming weeks he will be tested in the Primavera, so as to be able to compete against an even higher level of opponents.

Amorim is keeping an eye on him. Given his propensity for working with young players and instilling their trust, it cannot be ruled out that Jadid could appear on the list of players called up for a Serie A match in the near future.

For now, the parallel with Francesco Camarda – another record-holder from the Rossoneri youth team – is intriguing. Milan are enjoying him, and the Italian Federation are also monitoring things, as they could try to ‘steal’ him from Morocco.

#95334. Manchester City found guilty of 114 charges

Manchester City found guilty of 114 charges

📅 25 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2090 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester City have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League over breaches of its financial rules.
  • City face a range of sanctions from a fine to points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League.
  • If the verdict is upheld, with City expected to appeal, it will also raise question marks over the 20 trophies the club have won under Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, whose Abu Dhabi group took over in 2008.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester City have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League over breaches of its financial rules. It is a decision that, if upheld, would equate to one of the biggest scandals in football history.

City face a range of sanctions from a fine to points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League. Or a combination of all, under rule W51 of its handbook. No punishment has yet been announced.

If the verdict is upheld, with City expected to appeal, it will also raise question marks over the 20 trophies the club have won under Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, whose Abu Dhabi group took over in 2008.

The charges can be broken down into five categories and relate to a period from 2009-23 in which City won six League Cups, three FA Cups, seven league titles and the Champions League. There is the provision for removing past titles, but that would appear remote.

City have been the dominant force in English football for most of that time, but that status is under threat with a verdict that will send shockwaves around Europe and could have huge ramifications for the club.

That is unless they can win an appeal, with sources cautioning it still may take up to another two to three years for the case to be resolved, following on from an already five-year investigation.

The Premier League’s rules provide for an independent appeal board with broad powers, including the ability to uphold, vary or overturn the independent commission’s decision.

Recent findings suggest that it would therefore appear that despite the verdict, the case is far from being resolved and punishment decided. The details of the commission’s findings, when published, will be crucial to determining what happens next.

But if it is upheld, the verdict also opens up the possibility of City facing legal action from other clubs who feel they missed out on trophies and even merit money from league placings.

It is understood Premier League clubs are already discussing legal action and possible compensation claims as a result of the guilty verdict.

Each of those cases would have to be held individually, potentially leading to years more of litigation. Conversely, if City win their appeal, they too could take legal action against the Premier League the damage caused to their reputation.

Industry observers note that there has not yet been an official confirmation of the independent panel’s verdict from the Premier League. The Premier League declined to comment.

However, several sources have told Telegraph Sport that the panel has found City guilty of all but one of the charges they faced. The one that has not been proved is noted to be one of the most serious of the 115.

The damning verdict for City is a major newly introduced test of fragile UK relations with the United Arab Emirates, with whom bilateral trade was worth £25bn last year. Redacted freedom of information documents, seen by Telegraph Sport, show Abu Dhabi hosted UK government officials including Lord Stockwood, then investment minister, as recently as February. Khaldoon Al Mubarak, the City chairman and trusted adviser to the UAE president, was present at the meeting. Government notes from the meeting recorded that he “noted they are very proud of what they have achieved through their investments in Manchester”.

The Government previously caused acrimony among senior leaders in Abu Dhabi after putting forward legislation to ban foreign states from owning UK newspapers and news magazines. The intervention prompted the collapse of a takeover of The Telegraph in April 2024, which was largely funded by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the owner of City and vice-president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates.

It has been revealed that the previous UK government has admitted its embassy in Abu Dhabi and the Foreign Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) in London discussed the charges levelled at City by the Premier League. However it refused to disclose the correspondence.

Sources indicate that city have steadfastly maintained they are innocent, promising “irrefutable” evidence in support of their position, and had assembled some of the most expensive lawyers in the country to argue their case. Despite the verdict, the club are understood to be confident that it will win the argument in the end. Senior figures are noted to be calm about the latest development, as significant as it seems.

Industry observers note that city rebuilt their team this summer and it is understood that signings were brought in on conventional player contracts, rather than terms including clauses triggered in the event of a heavy punishment. Given the club have consistently denied breaching financial regulations, and their deals for newly introduced players to work with head coach Enzo Maresca underlines their position.

On Friday, a City spokesman said: “The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such, Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the club’s statement of February 2023.

“The club have diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.”.

Sources close to Pep Guardiola, the former City manager who stepped down last summer after 10 years of remarkable success at the club, including a treble triumph in 2023 and an unprecedented fourth straight league title in 2024, insist he has not been informed of any verdict.

In the days after City were first charged, Guardiola mounted a fierce defence of the club, claiming: “I am fully convinced we will be [proved] innocent.”.

The verdict vindicates the Premier League’s decision to launch an investigation after explosive allegations that City had routinely broken financial rules were first made in Der Spiegel in 2018 based on the Football Leaks documents.

Uefa previously accused City of breaches of its financial regulations and confirmed in 2020 that it was suspending the club from the Champions League for two years for “overstating” sponsorship revenue between 2012 and 2016.

Industry observers note that city denied the Uefa charges and, after an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, the two-year ban was overturned. Cas found that a number of the claims brought by Uefa had fallen outside a five-year “time bar” and others were “not established”.

It did, however, still impose a €10m fine after ruling that City failed to cooperate with investigators. City had previously also agreed a settlement with Uefa of €20m in 2014 following an investigation into their finances.

Recent findings suggest that legal experts agreed that the commission’s verdict is far from the end of the case. Yasin Patel, barrister at Church Court Chambers, remarked: “City’s lawyers will now analyse this decision and look at the options open to them to appeal, which may include procedural impropriety, wrongful interpretation of law, and legal errors – importantly, they can guarantee an appeal.

“Sanctions could include a major fine, points deduction, relegation or even all three. Factoring in whether titles and trophies should be stripped, whether other clubs have been robbed of further revenue and opportunities due to City’s wrongdoings and losses incurred, we safely say that this is only the first chapter of a long-running legal saga that will not end any time soon.”.

Ian Hargreaves, partner with specialist disputes firm Quillon Law, noted the verdict was “not the end of the story but the beginning of a new phase”, and added: “There is also the question of whether the panel’s decision can withstand a hard-fought appeal, and on what grounds any challenge might be brought. Much will depend on the detail of the panel’s findings and reasoning, which will inevitably be closely scrutinised by both sides.”.

Former Manchester City midfielder Rodri, who won the Ballon d’Or during his trophy-laden spell at the club, noted he believed the club were innocent.

Industry observers note that “For the players, it’s different than it is for journalists. I can understand all opinions, but we try to stay positive,” the Spain midfielder said while on international duty.

Industry observers note that “When you see all the people who worked hard at City to achieve success, you know what we achieved can’t be taken away. It wasn’t paid for with money, but with effort and teamwork. Everything we achieved was deserved; we marked one of the great eras of English football. I believe in the club’s innocence – we already went through this in 2020.”.

Andy Burnham, the Prime Minister, remarked: “I think we would all need to study the independent commission’s report in some considerable detail before reaching any conclusions.”.

Zohran Kwame Mamdani, the mayor of Fresh York, posted “114” in relation to the charges while former Manchester United players David de Gea and Rio Ferdinand both asked whether they should be due winner’s medals from past seasons.

The Premier League statement in February 2023 noted that “a number of alleged breaches” had been referred to an independent commission. It then detailed each specific rule against each season in which the alleged breach took place. The precise number was not clear from the statement and led to varying reports between 115 and 130. Friday’s news suggested the figure was 115.

Recent findings suggest that all the way to 2009-10, the first full season following the club’s takeover by Sheikh Mansour, who is a member of the Abu Dhabi Royal family and the vice president of the United Arab Emirates. There were charges relating to all 14 seasons until the Premier League completed their investigation during the 2022-23 campaign. In that time, City won seven Premier League titles, six League Cups, three FA Cups and the Champions League. They have since won another league title – the first club to do so four times in a row – as well as the Uefa Super Cup, the Fifa Club World Cup and the FA Cup and League Cup double last season.

Industry observers note that they can be split into five groups. The biggest relates to the seasons from 2009-10 until 2017-18 and the requirement for clubs to provide accurate financial information and act in the utmost good faith.

The next set of rules concern the full disclosure of manager and player payments. The alleged manager breaches related to the period between 2009-10 and 2012-13, when Roberto Mancini was leading the team. The alleged breaches with respect to player payments relate to all of the seasons between 2010-11 and 2015-16.

Recent findings suggest that as well as providing financial detail, clubs were required to meet Uefa and Premier League rules which were designed to bring a club’s spending broadly in line with their income by placing set limits on losses. City were charged with breaches of Uefa’s licencing and financial fair play rules from 2013-14 until 2017-18, and the Premier League’s profit and sustainability rules from 2015-16 until 2017-18.

The final set of charges spanned the five seasons during which City were being investigated by the Premier League and rules that require members to cooperate in the utmost good faith by providing information and documents.

A full picture will only emerge when the commission publishes its findings but we know that the Premier League investigation began in December 2018 following allegations in the German newspaper Der Spiegel based on the Football Leaks documents. These included alleged payments to former manager Mancini for consultancy work at an Abu Dhabi-based club that was separate to his regular contract at City.

Industry observers note that we also know that City were alleged to have breached rules over setting out image rights payments to players in their club contract. Der Spiegel reported that the Premier League investigation also focused on payments to under-age players, as well as whether club sponsors were paying for commercial deals themselves or a significant proportion was in fact effectively coming from owner Sheikh Mansour.

In a recent development, city have always denied breaking any rules. In response to the Premier League statement about the alleged breaches, they said that they have “irrefutable evidence” to support their position and “look forward to this matter being put to rest once and for all.”.

At the start of the hearing in September 2024, Guardiola also mentioned: “Wait for the independent panel. We believe we have not done anything wrong.”.

Of the Football Leaks documents, City stated: “We will not be providing any comment on out-of-context materials. The attempt to damage the club’s reputation is organised and clear.”.

By Adepoju Marvellous | 20 Nov 2026 15:36, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 19:58.

Two teams at opposite ends of the Eredivisie table meet on Sunday as FC Twente welcome Willem II to De Grolsch Veste.

The hosts are aiming for a fourth consecutive win in this fixture to remain within touching distance of their title rivals, while the visitors are desperate for a victory to spark what has been an underwhelming campaign so far.

Twente’s 2-2 draw against Ajax just before the break saw their four-game winning run come to an end, but given they were 2-0 down midway through the second half, securing a share of the spoils resoundingly feels like a point earned rather than two lost.

Just two points behind current leaders PSV Eindhoven, John van den Brom’s side remain firmly in the title race. While they trail Feyenoord, PSV, and Ajax in goals scored, they boast the league's best defence with just 12 goals conceded, and only Heerenveen have kept more clean sheets.

Three weeks after recording their largest-ever win - a 9-0 thrashing of SBV Excelsior - the Tukkers have a chance to lay down another marker against the division’s bottom club. Given rising expectations, a victory here feels almost non-negotiable.

On a personal note, Van den Brom will also want to preserve his impressive record against this weekend’s opposite number; across their previous 11 meetings, the Twente boss has recorded seven wins and four draws.

After winning each of their first home league matches this term, Sunday’s hosts have collected just one point from their last two outings and now seek to avoid going three straight Eredivisie matches in Enschede without a win for the first time since April 2025.

Willem II ended a run of six consecutive league defeats with a 1-1 draw against PEC Zwolle on November 6, but their wait for a first victory continues, as the appointment of Jurgen Streppel has yet to yield the desired turnaround.

It has been revealed that streppel returned for a second spell to replace John Stegeman, who managed just two points from a possible 27 over nine matches. The Zwolle stalemate was only Willem II's third point of the season, at least six fewer than any other team.

It has been revealed that already 12 points worse off than at this stage of their 2024-25 relegation campaign, De Superkruiken face a herculean task to avoid the drop. Upcoming fixtures against Twente and Feyenoord - two of the current top four - over the next three gameweeks only add to their challenge.

A league-high 40 goals conceded means Willem II are frequently punished for their league-low 11 goals scored. Consequently, there must be drastic improvement at one end of the pitch if they are to turn things around.

Facing a team that have scored 14 goals in the final 30 minutes of matches, Sunday’s hosts cannot afford to lose focus in a period in which they have conceded 19 goals, just under half of their season total.

Willem II form (all competitions):.

Max Bruns has not featured for Twente since September and remains unavailable, one of two defenders out of contention alongside Stav Lemkin, with the Israeli international suffering a long-term injury just before the start of the season.

Twenty-year-old Filip Erik Thorvaldsen is set to miss a sixth consecutive game for the hosts, who are also still without first-choice goalkeeper Lars Unnerstall.

Wout Weghorst is one of four players tied on nine goals in the Golden Boot race, and the striker will be eager to add to his tally.

Justin Hoogma (knee) and Amine Lachkar (groin) are Willem II’s two guaranteed absentees for Sunday’s clash, with the latter sidelined since July 2025.

However, French shot-stopper Thomas Didillon could also miss out for the away side, having featured just once since mid-August.

Drommel; Van Rooy, Propper, Nijstad, Adelgaard; Zerrouki, Weidmann; Rots, Taha, Orjasaeter; Weghorst.

Delanghe; Tjoe-A-On, Dekker, Stam, Ter Avest; Twigt, Zarrouk; Van Crooy, Van Aalst, Vilhena; Haen.

By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.

Published: 19:00 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 02:46 EST, 19 November 2026.

Mykhailo Mudryk has blamed his stint with the Ukrainian national team for the failed doping test which cost him two years of his career and revealed how fighting his case personally cost him millions of pounds.

The Chelsea winger, who is now on loan with Tottenham Hotspur, has opened up for the first time since he returned to football in the summer when his suspension was suddenly lifted.

Sources indicate that it was in a two-hour interview with Ukrainian journalist Dmitry Gordon via his YouTube channel. While the title of the video mentions ‘suicidal thoughts’, Mudryk clarifies during the conversation that he did not consider committing suicide despite being in a dark place. ‘Kill myself – no, that’s not a way out,’ he remarked when asked that question.

In a recent development, but he did discuss how Chelsea broke the news of his failed test to him, whether they helped their £89million signing from Shakhtar Donetsk during his ban, his belief that the drug meldonium entered his system while he was in Ukraine, and why he is now with Tottenham. He further claimed that he has faced threats from gangsters, and admitted his dream is to someday win the Ballon d’Or.

According to recent reports, on the Ukrainian national team and their federation, the Ukrainian Association of Football, Mudryk mentioned: ‘I’ll be honest, it pretended to help. But in reality, there was no help. They created more problems than they solved. Especially when we needed help the most, they turned their backs on us.

'I just would like, for the future, everyone to understand that you can only rely on yourself.'.

Mykhailo Mudryk has spoken publicly for the first time about the doping case that cost him two years of his career.

Mudryk has criticised the Ukrainian Association of Football over their support during his case.

Daily Mail Sport contacted the Ukrainian Association of Football for comment.

Continuing, Mudryk mentioned: ‘The UAF is afraid of being left to blame in this situation, and afraid of the criticism or whatever else might come raining down. Distancing themselves from their own player, not helping, pretending to help, and in the end, first they drag the case out for months without really helping the case in the end. But at least the UAF isn’t to blame.’.

It has been revealed that mudryk was handed an initial four-year ban after being charged by the Football Association for failing a doping test, with his last appearance prior to that coming in November 2024 in the Conference League away at Heidenheim. He scored in that 2-0 win for Chelsea. He was able to return when a seismic resolution was struck after changes to the 'scientific reporting standards'. Mudryk appeared for Chelsea during their pre-season tour before joining Tottenham on loan.

Recent findings suggest that on how and why he failed his test, Mudryk noted: ‘I had never heard of a drug like meldonium, never seen it, never come across it in my life. I only learned about it when they told me the news. I definitely have ideas. It’s a drug you can only get in Eastern Europe.

Industry observers note that ‘This drug could only have got into my body where I was, and that’s Ukraine. There are no such drugs in England. It supposedly stimulates your heart and helps you, as far as I understand, handle physical load better.

‘I was at home and Chelsea’s management came to see me and they said we needed to talk. Then they say you’ve returned a positive doping test and now you’re facing a ban.

Recent findings suggest that ‘You can’t believe it’s true. You can’t believe this is happening to you. If I’d ever taken anything anywhere, I’d have understood that this conversation might happen one day.

‘At least I’d have understood it was possible. But when you spend a huge pile of money on watching your diet, on a nutritionist, on a chef. When you spend that much money every year on all these things, that’s the last thing you expect. Because it speaks for itself: that you take things very seriously, like nutrition, everything that goes into your body, you watch it very closely.

‘Otherwise there’d be no need to spend money on it, because you could manage without it. They tell you this news, and you sit there, and you kind of listen to them but don’t hear them.

Mudryk returned to action when his ban was lifted in August, with the winger revealing Xabi Alonso told him to get game time and that he was 'counting on him'.

The Ukrainian joined Tottenham on loan but has seen injury restrict his involvement to date.

‘At some point you just go into a trance. It feels like you’re falling in a dream off a skyscraper. You’re flying down, you feel yourself flying down, and only in a dream do you wake up when you hit the ground, but in real life you don’t wake up, you just keep falling. It hits you very hard mentally. At that moment the tears came later.’.

Mudryk revealed how ‘the figure is in the millions’ when asked about the lawyers fees which were needed to fight his case. He confirmed he paid for that himself, along with the personal trainers and massage therapists he used to maintain his fitness while suspended. However, Mudryk did add that Chelsea continued to pay his salary during his time out of football.

On joining Tottenham and being reunited with Roberto De Zerbi, who formerly managed him at Shakhtar Donetsk, Mudryk mentioned: ‘It’s a perfectly logical decision. The club (Chelsea) has a latest coach (Xabi Alonso), he sees football his own way. He sees the players he needs for that football. He came up and told me straight to my face: “You’d better go and play, get some game time, and then come back to Chelsea. I’m counting on you.”’ On De Zerbi, he added: ‘We met and he says: “Are you happy? Come on, we’ve still got a lot of work to do together.”’.

Mudryk added how difficult it was after switching to England and, along with encountering problems with his former representatives who encouraged him to move to Chelsea rather than Arsenal, he said: 'They give you ultimatums, you know. That’s how it is.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 20 Nov 2026 15:39.

Real Madrid are reportedly preparing to secure the future of an out-of-favour attacker with an extraordinary £880m release clause, despite his limited involvement under Jose Mourinho this season.

Morocco international Brahim Diaz is said to have agreed a latest contract until June 2031, potentially extending his stay at the Santiago Bernabeu by another four years.

According to Spanish television programme El Chiringuito, the agreement includes a €1bn (£880m) release clause, with an official announcement expected next week.

Journalist Marcos Benito claims the 27-year-old signed the extension approximately two weeks ago, although Madrid have yet to confirm the arrangement publicly.

The reported deal is particularly striking given Brahim's position in Mourinho's squad, where he has struggled to secure regular opportunities despite contributing three assists this season.

His long-term future may be approaching a resolution, but his immediate prospects of becoming a first-team regular appear considerably less certain.

Brahim's existing agreement is due to expire in June 2027, making his future a subject of considerable speculation during the opening months of the campaign.

Real Madrid have been working to retain the versatile attacker, who returned from a three-year loan spell at AC Milan in 2023 and has provided valuable attacking depth in recent seasons.

However, he has found opportunities increasingly difficult to secure since Mourinho took charge.

The former Manchester City youngster has made nine appearances across all competitions in 2026-27, starting only twice and accumulating just 249 minutes of playing time.

His average of fewer than 28 minutes per appearance underlines the limited nature of his involvement, while he has started the last 11 matches on the bench.

Brahim has nevertheless contributed three assists, demonstrating that he can still influence matches during relatively brief appearances.

Competition for attacking positions has become particularly demanding.

Arda Guler has established himself as a more prominent member of Mourinho's aims, while Jude Bellingham and summer signing Yan Diomande occupy important roles in Madrid's attacking structure.

Vinicius Junior's anticipated return from suspension and Rodrygo's recovery from injury could further complicate Brahim's attempts to secure additional minutes.

The situation has already prompted questions about his future.

Earlier this month, Sports Mole reported on Brahim's prolonged spell among the substitutes and the growing concerns surrounding his lack of playing time.

Despite those difficulties, Mourinho has reportedly supported the club's efforts to retain the Morocco international.

The proposed extension would strengthen Madrid's contractual position considerably, although a release clause of €1bn should not be interpreted as a realistic valuation or asking price.

Such figures are frequently included in contracts at major Spanish clubs to provide protection against unwanted departures.

There is, however, some uncertainty surrounding the precise duration of Brahim's latest deal.

While El Chiringuito reports an agreement until 2031, Spanish newspaper AS has suggested that his renewal is arranged until 2030.

Neither version has been officially confirmed by Real Madrid.

Securing a new contract would represent a significant commitment from Madrid, but it would not guarantee Brahim a more substantial role in the team.

His position is particularly intriguing given that the club have several established attacking options and continue to develop younger players competing for similar positions.

For Brahim, the challenge is to turn occasional contributions into a more consistent place in Mourinho's starting XI.

That question also has implications for Morocco, where the midfielder remains an key international despite his restricted opportunities in Spain.

The Atlas Lions are building towards the 2030 World Cup, which Morocco will co-host alongside Spain and Portugal.

National team coach Mohamed Ouahbi has previously expressed a desire to see his players become more influential at club level, while acknowledging Brahim's ability to make a difference for his country.

Former Morocco international Mustapha Hadji has taken a stronger position, publicly questioning whether such limited club involvement is compatible with regular international selection.

Brahim's reported extension therefore raises an obvious sporting dilemma.

Remaining at the Bernabeu offers the prospect of competing for major trophies and retaining his place at one of Europe's most prestigious clubs.

However, the attacking competition that has restricted him to just two starts this season is unlikely to disappear simply because his contractual future is secured.

The deal would also make a potential departure more complicated, with interested clubs likely to require negotiations with Madrid rather than having the opportunity to sign him as a free agent next summer.

There is no indication that Brahim has asked to leave, and his reported decision to extend his contract suggests that he remains committed to fighting for his place.

For Mourinho, the challenge is different: finding sufficient opportunities for a talented squad player whom Madrid appear determined to retain for the long term.

An official announcement could settle the uncertainty surrounding Brahim's contract, but his limited involvement on the pitch remains a separate issue that the latest agreement cannot resolve.

Scotland’s ramped-up second-half performance offered some cause for optimism as Sébastien Pocognoli’s tenure as head coach began with a goalless draw with Slovenia in Ljubljana.

The 39-year-old Belgian head coach, appointed in August as Steve Clarke’s successor, refreshed the side for the Nations League Group B1 opener in the Stozice Stadium, but they were fortunate on a couple of occasions at least not to fall behind before rallying before the break.

Scotland had been insipid and uninspiring for most of the first half but after the interval they played with pace and purpose as Slovenia captain and goalkeeper Jan Oblak became a key figure, making saves from Oli McBurnie and Kieron Bowie.

Oli McBurnie spurns a chance for Scotland.It remains goalless between Slovenia and Scotland.📺 Watch on BBC One pic.twitter.com/sldzhNCGGb.

“It took us a bit of getting used to in the first half, the way the gaffer wants to play,” McBurnie told BBC Scotland.

Recent findings suggest that “We created enough chances to win the game. I should have scored. I was asked to play a different position and I enjoyed it. I’d rather be getting in the positions than not getting chances.

“Second half was a lot more of what the manager wanted from us. It was waves of pressure and the only thing missing was a goal or two.”.

However, the goal that would have made the former Union Saint-Gilloise and Monaco manager’s debut as an international boss more memorable ultimately failed to arrive.

In this extended international break, the Scots will host Switzerland at Hampden on Tuesday and then travel to North Macedonia before taking on Slovenia in Glasgow, with the Tartan Army hoping to see further improvement – and goals.

September 29: Scotland vs Switzerland.

October 3: North Macedonia vs Scotland.

October 6: Scotland vs Slovenia.

November 13: Scotland vs North Macedonia.

November 16: Switzerland vs Scotland.

Speaking to BBC Scotland, the debutant said: “Thought we struggled to get into the game first half, but second half we completely dominated the game.

“They’ve got a top goalie who made really good saves. So many positives to take and a clean sheet as well.

“We changed shape a wee bit at half-time to get more control and that did really well for us.

“It’s a significant game again on Tuesday so it’s important to recover now and go again.

“I’ve played on the left-hand side for a couple of years now, so I’m comfortable doing that.

Sources indicate that “We’ve had a great week. A new manager, new way of playing and new faces in camp. It’s just the chances we need to take - the fact we’re creating the chances stands us in good stead.”.

The striker told BBC Scotland: “It took us a bit of getting used to in the first half, the way the gaffer wants to play.

“We created enough chances to win the game. I should have scored.

Recent findings suggest that “I was asked to play a different position and I enjoyed it. I’d rather be getting in the positions than not getting chances.

“Second half was a lot more of what the manager wanted from us. It was waves of pressure and the only thing missing was a goal or two.”.

Pocognoli’s first game in charge of Scotland ends in a goalless draw. The visitors produced a dominant second-half display, but their final ball and end-product was severely lacking in crucial moments. Ure, Hickey, Gilmour, McBurnie and Bowie all came close to scoring, but no one could break the deadlock.

Scotland cannot find a way past the impenetrable Oblak. There will be just two minutes of added time for the visitors to possibly score a late winner.

Lovric clatters into Gilmour and is cautioned. Slovenia can’t get out. It’s wave after wave of Scottish pressure.

According to recent reports, oblak comes out and fails to claim Robertson’s free-kick. The ball is recycled and the Tottenham full-back whips a second cross into the box and Slovenia fail to clear. Welsh is waiting for it, but lashes a first-time volley over the bar.

Karnicnik catches Robertson with a late lunging tackle and receives a yellow card, giving Scotland a chance to get the ball into the box.

The hosts make their fifth alteration of the afternoon, with Cerin withdrawn and Lovric on instead.

Industry observers note that the second half has started as the first ended, with Scotland applying all of the pressure. Slovenia have Oblak to thank for the goalless scoreline.

McBurnie and Oblak both challenge for the ball, with the Scotsman bumping into the goalkeeper, giving Slovenia a goal kick. The decision is met by a chorus of boos from the away fans.

We are back under way for the second half. Both sides are unchanged at the break.

Pocognoli’s Scotland finished the half as the better side, but an opening goal has proved to be elusive. At times, they’ve looked suspect defensively and have lacked rhythm going forward. Despite Scotland’s late push for an opening goal at the end of the first half, the two sides head in level at the break. Slovenia started on the front-foot, with Sporar and Drkusic both going close for the hosts, before Ure struck the post to be denied a dream debut goal.

Angus Gunn remains his country’s first-choice goalkeeper.

“The first game is always a special game so you have to bring the mental aspect in for the players and for the staff.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this UEFA Nations League B, Group 1 match as Slovenia host Scotland at Stozice Stadium in Ljubljana.

Recent findings suggest that scotland qualified for their first World Cup in 28 years this summer, but they exited the tournament with a whimper after failing to finish as one of the best third-place group sides. Steve Clarke’s men beat tournament debutants Haiti 1-0 in their opening match, before falling to defeats without scoring against Morocco and Brazil.

Industry observers note that following the World Cup, Clarke stepped down as Scotland’s head coach, ending a seven-year tenure, and was replaced by Belgian manager Sebastien Pocognoli. The former Monaco boss will take charge of his first game in his fresh role today and will be itching to make an encouraging start in a new era for Scottish football.

Over this extended international break, Pocognoli’s side will also face Switzerland and North Macedonia, as well as a return fixture against Slovenia in Scotland on October 6 to round off a busy period.

While Scotland took part in the World Cup, Slovenia were reflecting on their hugely disappointing qualification performance, where they finished third in their group behind Switzerland and Kosovo without winning and netting just three goals across six matches.

Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko – Slovenia’s star man and most well-known player – withdrew from Bostjan Cesar’s squad earlier this week after the recurrence of a shin injury caused the 23-year-old to completely miss the 1-1 draw against Fulham last Sunday.

Scotland have a few notable absences, with Scott McTominay, Che Adams and Lawrence Shankland all unavailable, but Billy Gilmour returns to the fold after missing the World Cup through injury, Oli McBurnie has been recalled and Sevilla striker Robbie Ure has received his first senior call-up.

Kick-off is at 14:00, with team news coming shortly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 20 Nov 2026 16:12.

Unai Emery has confirmed that Matty Cash is one of three Aston Villa players who will miss Saturday's Premier League fixture against Sunderland.

Despite the Spaniard receiving rave reviews in recent months, Villa return from the November international break on a four-match winless streak.

Twice giving up a two-goal lead at Manchester United in their most recent game has left Villa in 10th place in the Premier League table.

With a Champions League showdown at Galatasaray to come on Tuesday, Emery must find a balance when naming his starting lineup for the game with the Black Cats.

Speaking at a press conference on Friday, Emery revealed that Cash would not be available.

While on international duty with Poland, Cash suffered a concussion during the fixture with Romania.

Meanwhile, Matteo Ruggeri and Amadou Onana - who signed a latest contract earlier this week - are also missing.

In a recent development, emery told reporters: "The players, more or less, they are good. Not so many changes with the players [out] injured.

"Of course, [Matty] Cash is [out with] concussion and Amadou Onana and Matteo Ruggeri they are both still out.

"Other players - they are ready.".

Although there was no mention of Aaron Wan-Bissaka after his recent injury, the expectation is that the Congo DR right-back will deputise for Cash.

Despite their exit from the EFL Cup, Villa still face a schedule that sees them playing seven times between November 21 and December 13.

Following the Sunderland and Galatasaray double-header, the West Midlands outfit play Ipswich Town, Everton, Crystal Palace, Paris Saint-Germain and Coventry City.

#95327. Industry News: Ferroptosis in cancer cells triggers PGE2 production for tumour immune escape

Industry News: Ferroptosis in cancer cells triggers PGE2 production for tumour immune escape

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 77 min read (15467 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~77 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, ferroptosis, a form of cell death induced by overwhelming membrane lipid peroxidation, is a vulnerability of many cancers, including cancers resistant to current molecular and immune-based therapies1,2,3,4,5,6,7.
  • Recent findings suggest that uncontrolled lipid peroxidation is integral to ferroptosis5,15.
  • Potentially relevant immunoregulatory factors produced by ferroptotic cancer cells are oxylipins, bioactive lipids generated through peroxidation of polyunsaturated fatty acid-containing membrane lipids, a hallmark of ferroptosis15.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, ferroptosis, a form of cell death induced by overwhelming membrane lipid peroxidation, is a vulnerability of many cancers, including cancers resistant to current molecular and immune-based therapies1,2,3,4,5,6,7. Triggering of ferroptosis therefore provides an opportunity to achieve elimination of difficult-to-treat cancers1,2,3,4,8,9. Studies in mouse cancer models have demonstrated that anticancer immunity, mediated by dendritic cells (DCs) and CD8+ T cells, is essential for effective tumour eradication by ferroptosis-inducing strategies10,11,12,13. However, ferroptotic cells limit this response8,9,10,14, resulting in immune escape and tumour growth through mechanisms that remain unclear. Here we demonstrate that ferroptotic cancer cells activate a molecular program resulting in aberrant production of prostaglandin E2 (PGE2), which limits the stimulation of anticancer CD8+ T cell responses by type 1 conventional DCs (cDC1s), thereby promoting immune escape. In ferroptotic cancer cells, lipid peroxidation-mediated membrane permeabilization enables Ca2+ influx, which activates p38 MAPK signalling and thereby drives PGE2 production. This signalling axis is uncoupled from cancer cell death and can be targeted to selectively interfere with immune-inhibitory PGE2 production while preserving ferroptotic cancer cell elimination. In the context of cancer cell ferroptosis, ablation of PGE2 production or disrupting PGE2 signalling restores cDC1-mediated anticancer CD8+ T cell responses and leads to effective tumour elimination. Our findings identify a key mechanism that limits antitumour immunity and prevents tumour elimination upon ferroptosis induction in cancer cells, which could be exploited for cancer therapy.

Recent findings suggest that uncontrolled lipid peroxidation is integral to ferroptosis5,15. Cancer cells are commonly protected from unrestrained lipid peroxidation and spontaneous ferroptotic cell death by molecular defence systems such as the system xc––glutathione (GSH)–glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) pathway5,16, in which GPX4 is the key enzyme mediating lipid peroxide detoxification. Strategies to promote ferroptosis by blockade of ferroptosis defence systems, such as GPX4 inhibitors, have been considered promising approaches to achieve tumour elimination in patients with difficult-to-treat cancers8,9. Studies using preclinical mouse models have uncovered that effective tumour elimination by ferroptosis-inducing strategies requires anticancer immunity by DCs10 and tumour-infiltrating CD8+ T cells11,12,13. Yet recent findings have suggested that DC-driven anticancer CD8+ T cell immunity is suppressed in ferroptotic tumours8,9,10,17. Emerging evidence has implicated that the unrestrained generation of membrane lipid peroxides in ferroptotic cells can promote the production and release of molecules that may impact immune cell functions18. However, what causes the suppression of DC-mediated anticancer CD8+ T cell immunity in the context of tumour ferroptosis remains largely unclear.

Potentially relevant immunoregulatory factors produced by ferroptotic cancer cells are oxylipins, bioactive lipids generated through peroxidation of polyunsaturated fatty acid-containing membrane lipids, a hallmark of ferroptosis15. To assess ferroptosis-induced oxylipin production and identify key factors, we profiled the oxylipin secretome of mouse BRAF(V600E) and NRAS(G12D) melanoma, 4T1 breast cancer and MC38 colorectal cancer cells following RSL3-induced ferroptosis. Across all these cancer cell lines, RSL3-treated (ferroptotic) cells displayed increased production of oxylipins compared with untreated (non-ferroptotic) controls (Fig. 1a). Of note, in all groups, the eicosanoid PGE2 was by far the most abundant oxylipin upregulated by ferroptosis induction (Fig. 1a). Similar to ferroptosis induction by RSL3 (which inhibits selenoproteins beyond GPX4), we observed strong PGE2 production after genetic ablation of the ferroptosis-protective enzyme GPX4, ferroptosis induction using the GPX4 inhibitor ML210 or erastin-mediated inactivation of system xc–-mediated cystine import (Extended Data Fig. 1a–f). Thus, ferroptosis may trigger the production of PGE2 in cancer cells, which is a notable finding given the crucial role of PGE2 for suppression of anticancer immunity19,20,21.

It has been revealed that a, Oxylipin profiles for the indicated cancer cell lines after RSL3 treatment. 4-HDHA, 4-hydroxydocosahexaenoic acid; 5,6-DHET, 5,6-dihydroxyeicosatrienoic acid; 6R-LXA4, 6R-lipoxin A4; 11-HETE, 11-hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acid; 15-oxoETE, 15-oxoeicosatetraenoic acid; DMSO, dimethyl sulfoxide; PDX, protectin DX; RvD1, resolvin D1; vs, versus. The vertical dotted line indicates a fold change (FC) (log2) of 0. b, PGE2 production by cancer cell lines after induction of ferroptosis, immunogenic cell death (ICD) or apoptosis. n = 4 samples for BRAF(V600E) melanoma, and n = 3 samples for NRAS(G12D) melanoma, 4T1 breast cancer and MC38 colorectal cancer. NS, not significant. c–f, Functional analyses of cDC1s exposed to dying cancer cell conditioned medium (CM). Experimental design (c). CXCL9 production by cDC1s; the plots show one cDC1 culture representative of n = 4 cultures (d). Quantification of CXCL9+ cDC1s, based on panel d; n = 4 samples (e). Analysis of cDC1s by RNA-seq (n = 4); the volcano plots show the effect of CM from ferroptotic (left) or apoptotic (right) BRAF(V600E) cells on activation-induced cDC1 genes (f). PE, phycoerythrin; RNA-seq, RNA sequencing; SSC-A, side scatter area. Data show mean ± s.e.m. of n = 3 biological replicates (a). In b, the centre line indicates the mean and the bounds show the minimum and maximum values. In e, the centre line indicates the median, the bounds extend from the 25th to the 75th percentile, and the whiskers correspond to he minimum and maximum values. P values are from one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) with Tukey’s multiple-comparison test (two-sided; b,e). Differentially expressed genes were identified using a two-sided Wald test with Benjamini–Hochberg correction (f).

By contrast, stimulation of ultraviolet B (UVB)-induced apoptosis, doxorubicin-induced immunogenic cell death or necrocide 1 (NC1)-induced necrotic cell death failed to promote PGE2 production (Fig. 1b and Extended Data Fig. 1g). However, PGE2 production was induced in cells undergoing necroptosis (Extended Data Fig. 1h). These findings imply that PGE2 production is selectively induced by as yet unknown molecular events in ferroptotic cells and that these events, at least to some extent, may be shared with necroptotic cells.

According to recent reports, using liproxstatin-1 (Lip-1), we further validated that ferroptotic cancer cells depend on lipid peroxides to produce PGE2 (Extended Data Fig. 2a,b). This was not the case for key effectors of other cell death pathways, such as caspases or receptor-interacting serine–threonine-protein kinase 1 (RIPK1; Extended Data Fig. 2a,b). We extended our analyses to a broader panel of mouse and human cancer cells, including established cell lines, cells from spontaneous mouse cancer models and cells from patients with pancreatic cancer. In all these cells, RSL3-induced ferroptosis triggered markedly increased PGE2 production (Extended Data Fig. 2c–e). Together, these data suggest that ferroptosis promotes aberrant production of PGE2 in mouse and human cancer cells, prompting us to investigate the underlying molecular mechanisms and consequences for anticancer immunity.

According to recent reports, effective anticancer immunity often depends on cDC1s22,23, which fulfil essential roles in the priming of anticancer CD8+ T cell responses24,25 and effector differentiation and expansion of CD8+ tumour-infiltrating T lymphocytes (TILs)26,27. These cDC1 functions are impacted by immunoregulatory factors derived from dying cancer cells22,23,28; however, how mediators released by ferroptotic cancer cells impact cDC1s and their functions is not known.

To address this issue, we generated cDC1s from bone marrow cells, exposed them to conditioned medium from RSL3-induced, ferroptotic BRAF(V600E) melanoma cells and assessed their functional properties after activation with polyinosinic–polycytidylic acid (poly(I:C); Fig. 1c). The conditioned medium from ferroptotic BRAF(V600E) cells strongly compromised the capacity of cDC1s to produce CXCL9 (Fig. 1d,e and Extended Data Fig. 3a), a chemokine required for cDC1-mediated orchestration of CD8+ TIL responses26,29. Similar results were observed for cDC1 production of the T cell stimulatory cytokine interleukin-12 (IL-12)30 (Extended Data Fig. 3b,c). By contrast, no impairment was observed for cDC1s exposed to conditioned medium from cancer cells undergoing apoptosis or doxorubicin-induced immunogenic cell death (Fig. 1d,e and Extended Data Fig. 3b,c). Impaired CXCL9 production was similarly observed for splenic cDC1s treated with conditioned medium from ferroptotic BRAF(V600E) cells (Extended Data Fig. 3d). These results suggest that factors released by ferroptotic cancer cells disable cDC1s from producing molecules required to promote anticancer CD8+ T cell immunity.

cDC1 functions are controlled by transcriptional programming31,32. We therefore subjected cDC1s activated by poly(I:C) following exposure to ferroptotic or apoptotic BRAF(V600E) cell conditioned medium to transcriptional profiling by RNA sequencing. We found that ferroptotic, but not apoptotic, cancer cell-derived factors induced prominent transcriptional changes in cDC1s (Fig. 1f), including impaired expression of genes encoding stimulatory cytokines (including Ifnb and Ifnl2), T cell-recruiting chemokines (Cxcl9 and Ccl4) and integrins notable for T cell activation (Itgal; Fig. 1f). We also confirmed the inhibitory effect on cDC1 cytokine and chemokine production at the protein level (Extended Data Fig. 3e). Of note, we did not detect a defect in upregulation of MHC or costimulatory molecules (Fig. 1f and Supplementary Table 1), implying that ferroptotic cancer cell-derived factors do not prevent cDC1 activation. Of note, many of the genes impaired in cDC1s following exposure to ferroptotic cancer cell-derived factors were shared with a core gene set of PGE2-mediated cDC1 dysfunction (Extended Data Fig. 3f,g and Supplementary Table 1), although genes beyond this set were also impaired. Consistently, gene set enrichment analyses revealed a prominent impairment of PGE2-regulated functional cDC1 genes (Extended Data Fig. 3h), whereas genes associated with migration or antigen processing (that is, molecular programs not regulated by PGE2 signalling in cDC1s19), remained unaffected (Extended Data Fig. 3h). Together, these data suggest that ferroptotic cancer cells promote cDC1 dysfunction and that this is mediated by PGE2.

It has been revealed that similar to cancer cells, ferroptosis induction caused aberrant PGE2 production in Pfa1 cells (Extended Data Fig. 4a), an established mouse embryonic fibroblast model often used to study the molecular underpinnings of ferroptosis33. This was linked to markedly increased transcript and protein expression of the key PGE2-producing enzyme COX2 (encoded by Ptgs2; Fig. 2a and Extended Data Fig. 4b–d). Lip-1 treatment rescued this effect (Fig. 2a), whereas stimulation of lipid peroxidation by cumene hydroperoxide promoted both Ptgs2 expression and increased PGE2 production in Pfa1 cells (Extended Data Fig. 4e,f). Together, these results point towards a requirement of membrane lipid peroxide generation for PGE2 production through transcriptional regulation of COX2. Using COX inhibitors, we also confirmed that COX activity was required for PGE2 production by ferroptotic Pfa1 cells (Fig. 2b), but dispensable for execution of ferroptotic cell death (Fig. 2c).
